BBa_261XH2RS.title: PliaG-RBS0-ccaS-m3-B0015
BBa_261XH2RS.description: This module consists of the engineered sensor kinase CcaS-m3 driven by the constitutive promoter PliaG, the RBS RBS0 and terminator B0015. When supplied with the chromophore phycocyanobilin (PCB) from the PCB Production Module [BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10), ccaS-m3 can detect green light and initiate signal transduction. Altogether, these components enable the conversion of external light stimuli into a regulatory signal for downstream gene expression.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

When supplied with the chromophore phycocyanobilin (PCB) from the PCB Production Module, ccaS-m3 can detect green light and initiate signal transduction.

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       PliaG (BBa\_K823000): the promoter of the *liaG* gene of *B. subtilis*, described in the Registry as a weak constitutive promoter and characterised as part of the Bacillus BioBrick Box (Radeck et al., 2013). It transcribes the downstream coding sequence without any added inducer.

·       RBS0 ([BBa\_26OSLRE4](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26oslre4)): the ribosome binding site, which sets translation initiation of the downstream coding sequence.

·       *ccaS-m3* (BBa\_K3317069): a miniaturised variant of *ccaS*, the cyanobacteriochrome histidine kinase of *Synechocystis* sp. PCC 6803. CcaS binds phycocyanobilin (PCB) through its GAF domain and phosphorylates the response regulator CcaR under green light. The variant corresponds to mini-CcaS#3 of Nakajima et al. (2016), in which the L1 linker and the two PAS domains are deleted and the GAF and histidine kinase domains are joined through a shortened linker.

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing past the coding sequence and prevents transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression of the CcaS light-sensing histidine kinase in the host *B. subtilis*.
* **Potential application:** Providing the green/red light input of the CcaSR system, as the light-sensing component of a stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor for plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**Light sensing:** Holo-CcaS is produced in a green light-sensitive ground state with low autokinase activity, with a photostate absorbance maximum at 535 nm. Absorption of a green photon switches CcaS to a red light-sensitive active state with high autokinase activity, with a photostate absorbance maximum at 672 nm. The active kinase transfers a phosphoryl group from ATP to a conserved histidine, and from there to a conserved aspartate on CcaR, which activates CcaR and induces transcription from the PcpcG2 output promoter. Red light reverts the active state to the ground state and de-activates PcpcG2 transcription, probably through CcaS-mediated dephosphorylation of CcaR (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019). The 535 nm and 672 nm are absorbance maxima of the CcaS photostates (Hirose et al., 2008), and are distinct from the illumination used in the published characterization, which was delivered by a Light Plate Apparatus with 520 nm green and 660 nm red LEDs (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019).

**Dependence on the PCB module:** CcaS is photoactive only as a holoprotein with PCB bound to its GAF domain, and *B. subtilis* does not make PCB natively. This module therefore has no function on its own. It depends on the PCB supply module PtagC+RBS-Ho1-pcyA-L3S2P21, which converts endogenous heme to biliverdin IXα and then to PCB inside the host. In the Level 2 system the two modules are carried together for this reason.

**Choice of the miniaturised variant:** We used *ccaS-m3* in place of full-length *ccaS*. The miniaturised variants of Nakajima et al. (2016) remove the two PAS domains, whose function in CcaS is not known, and several of them regulate gene expression better than the wild-type kinase. Castillo-Hair et al. (2019) tested *ccaSm3* and *ccaSm10* in *B. subtilis* PY79 and reported that both increased dynamic range about ten-fold, to 71 ± 12-fold for *ccaSm3* and 62 ± 12-fold for *ccaSm10*; the two were not statistically different in *B. subtilis* (p \= 0.49) and *ccaSm10* gave lower overall output, so the system containing *ccaSm3* was named *B. subtilis* CcaSR v1.0. The same PAS deletions applied in the *E. coli* CcaSR v2.0 context gave a v3.0 sensor four times less leaky, with a dynamic range of nearly 600-fold and no deleterious effect on green light sensitivity or response dynamics (Ong & Tabor, 2018). We took *ccaS-m3* as the better-supported choice on both counts, low background and high dynamic range.

**Promoter strength for the sensor:** The published system expresses *ccaS* from the xylose-inducible PxylA promoter and *ccaR* from the IPTG-inducible Phy-spank promoter (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019), so the levels of both proteins are set by chemical inducers (Haller et al., 2025). Our bioreactor is intended to run on light alone, without xylose or IPTG dosing, so we replaced the inducible promoter with a constitutive one. This substitution is our own design decision and is not part of the published system. We chose a weak constitutive promoter deliberately. Castillo-Hair et al. (2019) found that output falls again at high CcaS levels, probably because PCB becomes limiting and the resulting apo-CcaS has phosphatase activity. A weak promoter keeps CcaS inside the range where the PCB supplied by the PCB module can be loaded onto it. PliaG is one of the weaker σA promoters in the Bacillus BioBrick Box set, whose constitutive promoters span more than three orders of magnitude (Radeck et al., 2013).

sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The *ccaS-m3* coding sequence was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesised fragment using primers ccaS F and ccaS R. Each primer carries a 5' ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for Level 0 entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the start codon) at the 5' end and TGTC at the 3' end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into \[pGEM-T Easy] and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts PliaG (BBa\_K823000), RBS0 ([BBa\_26OSLRE4](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26oslre4)), *ccaS-m3* (BBa\_K3317069) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-1B-sfGFP Level 1 cloning vector (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

**DETAILS:**

* Composite insert: PliaG – RBS0 – *ccaS-m3* – B0015, \[1723 bp]
* Level 1 vector: pSTK-1B-sfGFP (Level 1 cloning vector), (ampicillin)
* Template: synthesised fragment
* Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification): \[60 °C]
* Assembly method: Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme
* Thermal cycle:

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-1B-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with pSTK-seq F and ccaSm3 R flanking the insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of \[1602 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, *ccaS-m3* CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 2 optogenetic system constructed in the pSTK-EXP2 vector.

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5' to 3') |                                                                    |
| ----------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
|             | ccaS F                     | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGG GAA AAT TTT TAA TTC CAA TT |
|             | ccaS R                     | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCT TAA GCT CGA GGC AAA TGG T  |
|             | pSTK-seq F                 | agtgccacctgacgtctaagaaacc                                          |
|             |                            |                                                                    |

## Results

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of \[pSTK-1B]-PliaG-RBS0-*ccaS-m3*-B0015.** \[X] of \[X] colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1602 bp]).

**Figure 2. Clone \[X] was sequence-verified and used for downstream experiments.**

BBa_262YYNPV.title: AcdS 2.1
BBa_262YYNPV.description: This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4; ; the wild-type acdS sequence is registered as [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi). It is an enzyme commonly found in plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of the plant hormone ethylene, thereby alleviating ethylene-induced growth inhibition in plants under stress. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## **About**

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 
*  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

## **Literature**

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

## **References**

1\. UniProt Consortium. (n.d.). *Q5PWZ8*. UniProt. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from[<u>UniProt entry Q5PWZ8</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5PWZ8/entry?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

2\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). ## **Literature**

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag** ([<u>**BBa\_26TOGLX3**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3))**:** The ACC deaminase protein is fused to the alpha-amylase signal peptide (SamyQ) at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus.**** 
* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26XVQ3FS**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xvq3fs)): this **Protectant Module** constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS, and terminator B0015.
* **PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26DE5E2Q**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26de5e2q)): this module includes the light-responsive promoter P*cpcG2*-veg, the RBS EEBD-RBS0, a protectant CDS, and the terminator B0015, which together drive the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in *Bacillus Subtilis* after[<u>BBa\_26XZYM10</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10),[<u>BBa\_261XH2RS</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs), and[<u>BBa\_26BDO8AQ</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq).
* **ccaSR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag** ([<u>**BBa\_26U8UTMH**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26u8utmh)): the system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control.

BBa_2654HAF3.title: ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag
BBa_2654HAF3.description: The system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control. The PCB Production Module ([BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10)) supplies the chromophore phycocyanobilin. The Light Sensing Module ([BBa\_261XH2RS](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs)) expresses CcaS-m3, which detects green light and autophosphorylates. The Transduction Module ([BBa\_26BDO8AQ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq)) expresses CcaR, which receives its phosphoryl group. Phosphorylated CcaR activates PcpcG2-veg in the Light-Responsive Expression Module ([BBa\_26Q3LKZU](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q3lkzu)), driving secretion of ACC deaminase via the Csn signal peptide. Expression is on in green light and off in red, giving external control over protein production instead of a constant burden on the cell.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This is the assembled Level 2 construct of our stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor. It carries four Level 1 transcriptional units on a single plasmid, so that *Bacillus subtilis* can sense and respond to light signals on its own. The first module makes the chromophore PCB, the second expresses the sensor kinase CcaSm3, and the third expresses the response regulator CcaR. The fourth is the output, which secretes ACC deaminase (AcdS) when green light is present - specifically, CcasR-Csn-AcdS-Histag (Bba\_2654HAF3), the wildtype output with the Csn signal peptide.

The part is a composite of four transcriptional units in this order: 

1. PCB production ([BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10)): PtagC + RBS ([<u>**BBa\_26A4MT29**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26a4mt29))-ho1:pcyA ([<u>**BBa\_K4354012**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k4354012) )-L3S2P21 ([<u>**BBa\_K2675031**</u>](https://share.google/pocPiJukHq9mm39e5)). Ho1 converts heme to biliverdin IXa, and PcyA subsequently reduces it to PCB. Fusing the two enzymes raises PCB production about 80 fold (Castillo-Hair et al. 2019). We used the shorter PtagC+RBS instead of Pveg and RBS0 to cut down repeated sequences and make Level 2 assembly easier .
2. Light Sensing ([BBa\_261XH2RS](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs)): PliaG (BBa\_K823000)-RBS0  (BBa\_26OSLRE4)- ccaS-m3 ([BBa\_26OSLRE4](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26oslre4))- B0015 (BBa\_B0015). This module expresses CcaSm3, the light sensor. Green light switches CcaS to an active state that passes a phosphate to CcaR, and red light switches it back.
3. Transduction ([BBa\_26BDO8AQ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq)): Pveg (BBa\_K143012) – RBS0 – ccaR (BBa\_K5431017) – B0015. When CcaS phosphorylates it under green light, CcaR binds the PcpcG2 promoter and activates transcription, and under red light it is likely dephosphorylated so that output switches off. Pveg keeps CcaR constitutively expressed, so light is the only input to the circuit. 
4. Light responsive ([BBa\_26Q3LKZU](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q3lkzu)): PcpcG2-veg – EEBD – RBS0 – Csn– AcdS – 6xHis ([BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)) – B0015. PcpcG2-veg is a strong promoter derived from Castillo-Hair et al. 2019, the Csn signal peptide directs ACC deaminase through the Sec pathway for secretion, where it degrades ACC, and the C-terminal 6xHis tag enables detection of the protein. 

This complete construct was assembled by Golden gate assembly into the Level 2 vector pSTK-EXP2 with BsmBI enzyme

## About

* Biosafety level: S1
* Target organism: *Bacillus subtilis* \[168/WB800]
* Main purpose of use: light controlled expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis*
* Potential application: controlling the release of plant growth promoting protectants with green and red light. Users can set stress thresholds for each crop through a microcontroller based sensor without redesigning the entire genetic circuit

## Literature

**How the circuit works:** CcaS binds PCB through its GAF domain and is made in a green-light sensitive ground state. Absorbing green light switches it to an active state that autophosphorylates and passes the phosphate to CcaR. Phosphorylated CcaR activates the PcpcG2 output promoter. Red light returns CcaS to the ground state and probably causes CcaS to dephosphorylate CcaR, which turns output off (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019; Hirose et al., 2008). Because *B. subtilis* does not make PCB, the circuit needs all four modules on the same plasmid to work. 

**Why optogenetic:** Our original plan was to release engineered rhizobacteria that sensed stress themselves, which limits the usable stressors, and crops also differ in their thresholds. For example, heat stress in *Arabidopsis* starts at about 30–37 °C, whereas peanut tolerates about 35–40 °C. Using light as the only input lets the user program thresholds per crop without redesigning the circuit. 

**Differences from the published system:** Castillo-Hair et al. (2019) drove *ccaS* from the xylose-inducible PxylA and *ccaR* from the IPTG-inducible Phy-spank. We replaced both with constitutive promoters (PliaG and Pveg) so that light is the only input and no inducer dosing is needed. 

**Output module:** PcpcG2-veg is promoter from Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), in which the sequence after the −10 hexamer comes from the strong Pveg promoter while the CcaR binding site stays intact. In the original study this gave much higher output than PcpcG2-172. The EEBD (*E. coli* expression-blocking device) sits upstream of the RBS to stop leaky expression of the output gene in *E. coli* during cloning, before the construct is moved into *B. subtilis*. The output gene is a fusion of a Sec signal peptide, *P. putida acdS*, and a 6xHis tag. In the SamyQ version, 12 of the first 15 *acdS* codons were recoded to open up the mRNA structure around the start codon.

## References

1. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Tabor, J. J. (2019). Optogenetic control of *Bacillus subtilis* gene expression. *Nature Communications*, 10, 3099.
2. Hirose, Y., Shimada, T., Narikawa, R., Katayama, M., & Ikeuchi, M. (2008). Cyanobacteriochrome CcaS is the green light receptor that induces the expression of phycobilisome linker protein. *PNAS*, 105(28), 9528–9533.
3. Caro-Astorga, J., Rogan, M., Malcı, K., Ming, H., Debenedictis, E., James, P., & Ellis, T. (2025). SubtiToolKit: A bioengineering kit for *Bacillus subtilis* and Gram-positive bacteria. *Trends in Biotechnology*, 43(6), 1446–1469.
4. Fernández, S., Ayora, S., & Alonso, J. C. (2000). *Bacillus subtilis* homologous recombination: Genes and products. *Research in Microbiology*, 151(6), 481–486.
5. Chen, Y.-J., et al. (2013). Characterization of 582 natural and synthetic terminators and quantification of their design constraints. *Nature Methods*, 10(7), 659–664.
6. Haller, D. J., Castillo-Hair, S. M., & Tabor, J. J. (2025). Optogenetic control of *B. subtilis* gene expression using the CcaSR system. *Methods in Molecular Biology*, 2840, 1–17.
7. Radeck, J., et al. (2013). The Bacillus BioBrick Box. *Journal of Biological Engineering*, 7, 29.

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

Each module was first built and sequence verified as a Level 1 transcription unit in the SubtiToolKit pSTK-1A, -1B, -1C, and -1D vectors (Caro-Astorga et al. 2025). The four sequence verified Level 1 units were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction into the pSTK-EXP2 Level 2 vector, in the order Module 1-Module 2-Module 3-Module 4. We tested two vectors to insert ratios, 1:5 and 1:7. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and clones were screened by colony PCR with primers specific to each module and sequence verified. The verified plasmid was then electroporated into *B. subtilis* 168 and WB800 at 2.1-2.3 kV 

Construct details:

* Composite insert: pSTK-EXP2-sfGFP-PtagC+RBS-Ho1:pcyA-L3S2P21-PliaG-RBS0-CcaSm3-B0015-Pveg-RBS0-CcaR-B0015-PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn:AcdS-Histag-B0015 
* Vector: pSTK-EXP2 (Level 2 vector)
* Assembly method: Golden Gate Assembly (BsmbI)
* Vector:insert ratios tested: 1:5 and 1:7
* Thermal cycle

| Temperature         | Time    | Cycles     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ---------- |
| 42 degrees Celcius  | 5 min   | 45 cycles  |
| 16 degrees Celcius  | 5 min   |            |
| 55 degrees celsius  | 10 min  | 1 cycle    |
| 80 degrees Celcius  | 20 min  | 1 cycle    |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the Level 2 transformation were screened by colony PCR, with primers specific to each module, and products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A colony was a positive candidate only if it gave a band of the expected size for the modules . Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that all four modules are correct and in the right order. We checked every module because one module being positive doesn’t necessarily verify the state of the others. Constructs that were confirmed were then electroporated into *B. subtilis* and grown into liquid culture to initiate full functional runs in the LPA. 

| Primer      | Sequence                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| L2-pcyA-F   | GCG AAG CAT GGG CAG AAA GA     |
| L2-ccaSm3 R | GCG TTC TTG GTT TTG TCT GTG CC |
| L2-ccaSm3 F | GGG AAC AGG ACT CGG TTT AAT GG |
| L2-ccaR R   | CCA GCG GCA AAT CAT CCT CC     |
| L2-ccaR F   | GGT CCA TGG CAT TGG GTA TCG    |
| L2-SamyQ R  | GAA CGA AAC TGT CCG CTT TCG TT |

## Results (wet lab)

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/e093103b-ab92-4883-9ac7-8f4160e8e942/ba762e02cb85ba4902ecfa6ff18b66b651548425f2a458b6af9b20c0fe8a7f08.avif)

**Fig. 1. Colony PCR verification of the ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag construct.** Lane M contains the DNA ladder, and lanes 2 through 5 represent individual colonies screened using ccaSm3 F and ccaR R primers. The electrophoresis results indicate that lanes 3, 4 and 5 yield a band migrating between the 500 and 750 basepair markers, consistent with the expected size of 632 basepairs, while lane 2 yields no product. The bright band near 250 basepairs and the faint higher-molecular-weight bands in lanes 3 through 5 are non-specific amplifications.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/e093103b-ab92-4883-9ac7-8f4160e8e942/1bb1bfecc9e21bdbf44520b10b23a3f8ee398d68e02016aa9958e874bdd453ed.avif)

**Fig. 2. Colony PCR verification of the ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag construct.** The gel indicates that both clones have correct bands across all 4 modules, confirming successful assembly.

The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and clones were screened by colony PCR with primers specific to each module and sequence verified. The verified plasmid was then electroporated into *B. subtilis* 168 and WB800 at 2.1-2.3 kV 

Construct details:

* Composite insert: pSTK-EXP2-sfGFP-PtagC+RBS-Ho1:pcyA-L3S2P21-PliaG-RBS0-CcaSm3-B0015-Pveg-RBS0-CcaR-B0015-PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn:AcdS-Histag-B0015 
* Vector: pSTK-EXP2 (Level 2 vector)
* Assembly method: Golden Gate Assembly (BsmbI)
* Vector:insert ratios tested: 1:5 and 1:7
* Thermal cycle

| Temperature         | Time    | Cycles     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ---------- |
| 42 degrees Celcius  | 5 min   | 45 cycles  |
| 16 degrees Celcius  | 5 min   |            |
| 55 degrees celsius  | 10 min  | 1 cycle    |
| 80 degrees Celcius  | 20 min  | 1 cycle    |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the Level 2 transformation were screened by colony PCR, with primers specific to each module, and products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A colony was a positive candidate only if it gave a band of the expected size for the modules . Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that all four modules are correct and in the right order. We checked every module because one module being positive doesn’t necessarily verify the state of the others. Constructs that were confirmed were then electroporated into *B. subtilis* and grown into liquid culture to initiate full functional runs in the LPA. 

| Primer      | Sequence                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| L2-pcyA-F   | GCG AAG CAT GGG CAG AAA GA     |
| L2-ccaSm3 R | GCG TTC TTG GTT TTG TCT GTG CC |
| L2-ccaSm3 F | GGG AAC AGG ACT CGG TTT AAT GG |
| L2-ccaR R   | CCA GCG GCA AAT CAT CCT CC     |
| L2-ccaR F   | GGT CCA TGG CAT TGG GTA TCG    |
| L2-SamyQ R  | GAA CGA AAC TGT CCG CTT TCG TT |

## Results (wet lab)

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/e093103b-ab92-4883-9ac7-8f4160e8e942/ba762e02cb85ba4902ecfa6ff18b66b651548425f2a458b6af9b20c0fe8a7f08.avif)

**Fig. 1. Colony PCR verification of the ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag construct.** Lane M contains the DNA ladder, and lanes 2 through 5 represent individual colonies screened using ccaSm3 F and ccaR R primers. The electrophoresis results indicate that lanes 3, 4 and 5 yield a band migrating between the 500 and 750 basepair markers, consistent with the expected size of 632 basepairs, while lane 2 yields no product. The bright band near 250 basepairs and the faint higher-molecular-weight bands in lanes 3 through 5 are non-specific amplifications.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/e093103b-ab92-4883-9ac7-8f4160e8e942/1bb1bfecc9e21bdbf44520b10b23a3f8ee398d68e02016aa9958e874bdd453ed.avif)

**Fig. 2. Colony PCR verification of the ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag construct.** The gel indicates that both clones have correct bands across all 4 modules, confirming successful assembly.

sections.title: Application
sections.original:
The Level 2 construct ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag (BBa\_2654HAF3) shows that *Bacillus subtilis* can sense light and respond to it on its own. All four modules sit on a single plasmid. The first makes the chromophore PCB, the second expresses the sensor kinase CcaS-m3, the third expresses the response regulator CcaR, and the fourth secretes ACC deaminase (AcdS) when green light is present. Because *B. subtilis* does not make PCB, the circuit only works with all four modules together.

We tested this in *B. subtilis* WB800 in the LPA (light plate apparatus) under green and red light at different intensities. Western blots showed ACCD signal increasing over time under green light, but not under red light. This is the proof of concept for the whole design: light is the only input, and no inducer needs to be added.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.original:
#### Use in plant protection

The aim is to release plant-protective proteins only when and where they are needed. A secreted ACC deaminase lowers stress ethylene around roots, so it could be used as part of a plant-growth-promoting bioprotectant. Light as the only input offers a practical advantage over circuits that sense stress themselves. Crops differ in their stress thresholds (for example, heat stress starts at about 30 to 37 °C in *Arabidopsis* but about 35 to 40 °C in peanut), and a self-sensing strain would have to be redesigned for each stressor and each crop. With light control, a user can set thresholds for each crop through a microcontroller-based sensor that switches the light, without redesigning the genetic circuit. This is the role the circuit plays in our bioreactor system.

#### A modular platform for other protectants

Modules 1 to 3 form a reusable light-sensing chassis, and only Module 4 defines the output. Any of our protectant cassettes can in principle be placed behind PcpcG2-veg:

* **AcdS** lowers ethylene levels. This is the version built and tested in the full circuit.
* **LEA14** protects cellular structures under environmental stress. We did not build the light-responsive Module 4 with LEA14. Instead, we characterized the constitutive LEA14 version to see how it would behave in the whole system, and it also protects plants facing salinity stress. This avoids repeating the same assembly, since ccaSR-AcdS already demonstrates that the concept works.
* **BoPep4**, a broccoli plant elicitor peptide, activates plant defense responses.

Our constitutive constructs, which use Pveg in place of the light switch, give the maximal secretion and production of each protectant. They also serve as a benchmark for the light-controlled version.

#### Beyond our project

Replacing the xylose-inducible and IPTG-inducible promoters of the published CcaSR system (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019) with constitutive ones means no inducer dosing is required. Other teams can reuse the four-module Level 2 plasmid for any secreted protein, simply by exchanging the output cassette. This makes light-controlled secretion in *B. subtilis* usable beyond plant protection, for example for other enzymes or peptides that should be produced on demand.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica).*

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (BBa\_K1074014):** N-terminal signal peptide of the amyQ gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in Bacillus subtilis (and related lineages like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **BoPep4 2.2 (**[<u>**BBa\_26ERHWWI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26erhwwi) **):** encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica),* with its native start codon removed, followed by a stop codon. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** fused N-terminally to the peptide. This allows detection and quantification of the short peptide after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety Level:** S1
* **Target organism:** Bacillus subtilis \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of BoPep4 in the host B. subtilis
* **Potential application:** Enhancing plant salt-stress tolerance as a component of plant-protecting bioprotectants

## Dry lab / computational analysis

The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and start codon influences translation-initiation efficiency inside bacteria, independent of the encoded protein sequence. Following the concept suggested by Castillo-Hair (2019), the design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 CDS as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 was used to generate and fold tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5′ window (residual recombination site + MF001 RBS + spacer + SamyQ ORF + first 90 nt of CDS), determining the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG), and combining these into a balance score.

Wild-type BoPep4 was the weakest starting point of the whole construct series: start+15 accessibility was only 0.396 and SD-core accessibility only 0.067, both below the \~0.50 usability threshold and the Ho1 reference baseline (0.681). SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag was determined to be the best candidate from the run: 9 of the first 15 BoPep4 codons were changed (c2 ATT→ATC, c5 GGA→GGT, c6 TCA→AGT, c7 AAA→AAG, c10 CCG→CCT, c11 AGA→AGG, c13 CCG→CCT, c14 CAT→CAC, c15 TCA→TCC). The predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.396 to 0.497, and SD-core accessibility rose sharply from 0.067 to 0.634 (roughly a 9.5-fold gain), resulting in an overall balance score gain of 0.462 to 1.131. The codon adaptation index in B. subtilis 168 dropped from 0.87 to 0.77. We verified this variant against a Castillo-rule-applied control (low GC content, A over U): the control reached a start+15 of 0.677 and an SD-core of 0.425 (balance 1.102) an improvement over wild type, but still below the balance achieved by individually folding and verifying each candidate.

## References

1. Wang, A., Guo, J., Wang, S., Zhang, Y., Lu, F., Duan, J., Liu, Z., & Ji, W. (2022). BoPEP4, a C-Terminally Encoded Plant Elicitor Peptide from Broccoli, Plays a Role in Salinity Stress Tolerance. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 23(6), 3090–3090. [<u>https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090</u>](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090)
2. Li, R., Liu, M., Hu, X., Li, J., Pang, Q., Yan, X., Li, J., & Ji, W. (2026). Broccoli plant elicitor peptide BoPep4 enhances plant salt tolerance by improving glucosinolate metabolism. Plant Science, 364, 112954.

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The SamyQ-Bopep4 2.2-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-SamyQ-Bopep4 2.2-Histag. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the SamyQ-Bopep4 2.1-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

Construct details:

* **Insert:** SamyQ signal peptide – Bopep4 2.2 – 6x Histag, \[177 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SamyQ F     | ATATAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA TTC AAA AAC GAA AGC GGA C |
| BoPep R     | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA TG   |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetized fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the SamyQ and STK R primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag insert \[177 bp] plus the vector sequence between the Histag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[536 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, BoPep4 2.2 coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/b566a2c3-8f38-4553-99a0-7f84e388a866/c99753738e9199f0b8df03c2cd933ef5b4924dd02a1b503b646bb6101bbfd98d.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-0C-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag**. The figure indicates that 4 of 4 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[536 bp])

**Figure 2. Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The SamyQ-Bopep4 2.2-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-SamyQ-Bopep4 2.2-Histag. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the SamyQ-Bopep4 2.1-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

Construct details:

* **Insert:** SamyQ signal peptide – Bopep4 2.2 – 6x Histag, \[177 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SamyQ F     | ATATAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA TTC AAA AAC GAA AGC GGA C |
| BoPep R     | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA TG   |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetized fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the SamyQ and STK R primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag insert \[177 bp] plus the vector sequence between the Histag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[536 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, BoPep4 2.2 coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/b566a2c3-8f38-4553-99a0-7f84e388a866/c99753738e9199f0b8df03c2cd933ef5b4924dd02a1b503b646bb6101bbfd98d.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-0C-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag**. The figure indicates that 4 of 4 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[536 bp])

**Figure 2. Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of the composite part:

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica).*

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       Pveg (BBa\_K143012): a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction.

·       EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)): a composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*.

·       SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26PX0UGH](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26px0ugh)): The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (BBa\_K1074014):** N-terminal signal peptide of the amyQ gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in Bacillus subtilis (and related lineages like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **BoPep4 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_26LYCBW0**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26lycbw0)**):** encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica),* with its native start codon removed, followed by a stop codon. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** fused N-terminally to the peptide. This allows detection and quantification of the short peptide after successful assembly and electroporation.

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete cassette was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of BoPep4
* **Potential application:** Enhancing plant salt-stress tolerance as a component of plant-protecting bioprotectants

## Literature

**Rationale.** BoPep4 is a 23-residue mature plant elicitor peptide from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea* var. *italica*), sequence GILIGSKKRPREPHSSGKPGGHN. It works through auxin and abscisic acid signalling crosstalk to raise salt-stress tolerance in broccoli, lowering the Na⁺/K⁺ ratio and promoting leaf wax and cutin accumulation (Wang, A., et al., 2022). This cassette carries the recoded BoPep4 2.1 coding sequence behind the SamyQ signal peptide, which directs the peptide into the Sec-dependent secretion pathway. The 6x Histag is fused N-terminally to the peptide, which allows detection and quantification of the short peptide.

**Why the recoded 5′ end.** The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and the start codon influences translation initiation in bacteria, independently of the encoded protein sequence. Following Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), our design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 coding sequence as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 (Lorenz et al., 2011) generated and folded tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5′ window (residual recombination site, MF001 RBS, spacer, SamyQ ORF and the first 90 nt of the CDS), scoring the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG) and combining the two into a balance score. Wild-type BoPep4 was the weakest starting point of the whole construct series, with start+15 accessibility 0.396 and Shine-Dalgarno core accessibility 0.067, both below the roughly 0.50 usability threshold and below the Ho1 reference baseline of 0.681, which is why this cargo had the most to gain. BoPep4 2.1 was the best candidate of the run. Nine of the first 15 BoPep4 codons were changed (c2 ATT→ATC, c5 GGA→GGT, c6 TCA→AGT, c7 AAA→AAG, c10 CCG→CCT, c11 AGA→AGG, c13 CCG→CCT, c14 CAT→CAC, c15 TCA→TCC). Predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.396 to 0.497 and Shine-Dalgarno core accessibility rose from 0.067 to 0.634, roughly a 9.5-fold gain, for a balance score gain of 0.462 to 1.131. The codon adaptation index against *B. subtilis* 168 usage (Kazusa DNA Research Institute, n.d.) dropped from 0.87 to 0.77. Instead of applying Castillo's rule, which prioritises low GC content and A over U, the pipeline folded and checked every candidate individually; the Castillo-rule control reached a start+15 score of 0.677 and a Shine-Dalgarno core score of 0.425 (balance 1.102), below the balance reached by individual verification. The encoded peptide sequence is unchanged. These scores are predictions. Translation initiation from this cassette has not been measured.

**Why three BoPep4 versions.** Our three BoPep4 cassettes, carrying wild-type BoPep4, BoPep4 2.1 and BoPep4 2.2, all use the SamyQ signal peptide and differ only in the first 15 codons. They are the one place in our part set where the effect of 5′ recoding can be read on its own, with everything else held fixed.

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression at a fixed level, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *Escherichia coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.



1\. Wang, A., Guo, J., Wang, S., Zhang, Y., Lu, F., Duan, J., Liu, Z., & Ji, W. (2022). BoPEP4, a C-terminally encoded plant elicitor peptide from broccoli, plays a role in salinity stress tolerance. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 23(6), Article 3090. [https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090)

2\. Caro-Astorga, J., Rogan, M., Malcı, K., Ming, H., Debenedictis, E., James, P., & Ellis, T. (2025). SubtiToolKit: A bioengineering kit for *Bacillus subtilis* and Gram-positive bacteria. Trends in Biotechnology, 43(6), 1446–1469. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004)

sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* **Composite insert:** Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag – B0015, \[906 bp]
* **Level 1 vector:** pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* **Template:** synthesized fragments assembled together
* **Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification):** 60 °C
* **Assembly method (Level 1):** Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* **Thermal cycle:**

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was cloned into pSTK-0C-sfGFP and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), SamyQ-BoPep 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26PX0UGH](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26px0ugh)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                                |
| SamyQ F        | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGATTC AAAAACGAAAGCGGAC             |
| BoPep R        | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA TG |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                                         |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with backbone primers primers flanking the CDS insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[678 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/eebe25ab-2090-4a56-92ea-26f9be11d10b/469dcae98058bf052c5d7026ee3448aa788dd36eb0a6ba6d0054ffd3a5eeecd7.avif)

***Figure 1.*** **Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag-B0015.** 1 of 10 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[678 bp]).

***Figure 2.*** **Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

BBa_26A4MT29.description: A standardized genetic part combining a bacterial promoter (PtagC) and a Ribosome Binding Site (RBS). This composite part provides control of both transcription and translation for a downstream gene of interest.

BBa_26BDO8AQ.title: Pveg-RBS0-ccaR-B0015
BBa_26BDO8AQ.description: This module consists of CcaR, the response regulator component of the cyanobacterial CcaS/CcaR two-component signaling system, along with the constitutive promoter Pveg, the RBS RBS0, and the terminator B0015. Acting as the intermediary between light perception and gene expression, CcaR receives the phosphoryl group from the green light-activated CcaS and activates transcription from the PcpcG2 promoter. Together, it enables the conversion of environmental light cues into a transcriptional response.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

The Transduction Module relays the light signal from the sensor to the gene expression module. It consists of ccaR, the response regulator of the cyanobacterial ccaS/ccaR two-component system. 

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       Pveg (BBa\_K143012): a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction.

·       RBS0 ([BBa\_26OSLRE4](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26oslre4)): the ribosome binding site, which sets translation initiation of the downstream coding sequence.

·       *ccaR* (BBa\_K5431017): the coding sequence of CcaR, the response regulator of *Synechocystis* sp. PCC 6803 that is cognate to the CcaS histidine kinase. Phosphorylated CcaR binds the operator region of the PcpcG2 promoter and activates transcription from it.

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing past the coding sequence and prevents transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression of the CcaR response regulator in the host *B. subtilis*.
* **Potential application:** Transducing the CcaS light signal to the PcpcG2-veg output promoter, as the signal transduction component of a stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor for plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**Signal transduction:** CcaS and CcaR form a two-component system. Under green light the active CcaS kinase transfers a phosphoryl group from ATP to a conserved histidine in its own kinase domain, and from there to a conserved aspartate on CcaR. Phosphorylation activates CcaR, which then induces transcription from the PcpcG2 output promoter. Red light reverts CcaS to its ground state and de-activates PcpcG2 transcription, probably through CcaS-mediated dephosphorylation of CcaR (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019). In the original description of the pathway, autophosphorylation of the CcaS histidine kinase domain is up-regulated by green light, and CcaS then phosphorylates CcaR, which induces *cpcG2* expression (Hirose et al., 2008). Replacing it with constitutive Pveg is our own decision, made so that light is the only input to the circuit and the bioreactor needs no inducer dosing. (2019) report that of all the cyanobacterial genes in their study *ccaR* was the only one that did not initially suffer from poor expression. Expressing CcaR constitutively also means its level no longer tracks an inducer, so it becomes a fixed property of the strain.

**Background activation of CcaR:** This design's main risk is on the CcaR side. In the published v0.1 system, adding IPTG alone, which raised CcaR without any green light, increased sfGFP output up to 40-fold, probably because CcaR can be phosphorylated by a small-molecule donor such as acetyl phosphate (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019). The amount of CcaR in the cell therefore sets how much output the circuit gives in the dark, and a constitutive promoter fixes that background. Dark-state and red-light output must therefore be measured for this module in our strain and reported alongside the green-light output; a fold-change quoted without a measured background would not be meaningful. These measurements have not yet been made. If the background proves too high, the correction is a weaker promoter or a weaker RBS on this module.

**Reuse of standard parts:** Pveg, RBS0 and B0015 are reused across our modules, which keeps every cassette in the same SubtiToolKit format and makes the Level 2 assembly straightforward (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025). sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The *ccaR* coding sequence was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesised fragment using primers ccaR F and ccaR R. Each primer carries a 5' ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for Level 0 entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the start codon) at the 5' end and TGTC at the 3' end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pGEM-T Easy and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), RBS0 ([BBa\_26OSLRE4](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26oslre4)), *ccaR* (BBa\_K5431017) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-1C-sfGFP Level 1 cloning vector (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

**CONSTRUCT DETAILS:**

* Composite insert: Pveg – RBS0 – *ccaR* – B0015, \[XXXX bp]
* Level 1 vector: \[pSTK-1C-sfGFP] (Level 1 cloning vector), \[marker to be confirmed]
* Template: synthesised fragment
* Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification): \[60 °C]
* Assembly method: Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* Thermal cycle:

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-1C-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with pSTK-seq F and pSTK-seq R flanking the insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the insert \[1174 bp] plus the vector sequence between the priming sites, for a total of \[1442 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, *ccaR* CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 2 optogenetic system constructed in the pSTK-EXP2 vector.

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5' to 3')                                         |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| ccaR F      | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA GAA TTC TTT TAG TGG AGG AT |
| ccaR R      | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCC TAG TTT TTC CCT TGG CAC AA |
| pSTK-seq F  | agtgccacctgacgtctaagaaacc                                          |
| pSTK-seq R  | tctttcctgc gttatcccct gattc                                        |

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/a624c01e-1fc3-4ecd-b13d-c2b08788b2f5/fa7885bfe062bde6a5b9dd458239954935da17bdf37c95e2f52b07f62a804a5c.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-1C-Pveg-RBS0-ccaR-B0015.** 2 of 4 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1442 bp]).

**Figure 2. Clone 2 was sequence-verified and used for downstream experiments.**

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS: [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a composite transcription unit with three elements, in this order:

* **Pveg (**Bba\_K143012**):** a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction. 
* **EEBD-RBS0 (**[BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)**):** A composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*
* **Csn-AcdS-Histag (**[BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)**):** a translational fusion of three elements:
  * **Csn signal peptide:** the N-terminal Sec-dependent signal peptide of *B. subtilis* chitosanase (gene *csn*), which directs the protein to the secretion pathway and is cleaved off during export.
  * **AcdS** ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)): the ACC deaminase coding sequence from *Pseudomonas putida*, with its native start and stop codons removed.
  * **6x Histag:** fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon, allowing protein detection and purification.
* **B0015** (BBa\_B0015): A high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of ACC deaminase
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**Rationale.** ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of ethylene, and so can lower the ethylene levels that inhibit plant growth under stress (Hontzeas et al., 2004; Shah et al., 1998). The Csn signal peptide exports the enzyme from the cell, and the C-terminal 6x Histag allows detection and purification. The AcdS sequence comes from Q5PWZ8 (UniProt Consortium, n.d.; GenBank CP053102.1).

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo rather than promoter strength. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *E. coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts, so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## References

1\. UniProt Consortium. (n.d.). *Q5PWZ8*. UniProt. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from[ <u>UniProt entry Q5PWZ8</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5PWZ8/entry?)

2\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). Expression and characterization of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase from the rhizobacterium pseudomonas putida UW4: A key enzyme in bacterial plant growth promotion. *Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, 1703(1)*, 11–19. PubMed.[ <u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015</u>](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

3\. Shah, S., Li, J., Moffatt, B. A., & Glick, B. R. (1998). Isolation and characterization of ACC deaminase genes from two different plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. *Canadian Journal of Microbiology, 44*(9), 833–843.[ <u>https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074</u>](https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074)

4\. Deng, L. (2022). *Bacillus subtilis subsp. subtilis str. 168 chromosome, complete genome* \[GenBank sequence CP103783.1]. GenBank. National Center for Biotechnology Information.[ <u>https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nucleotide/CP103783.1</u>](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nucleotide/CP103783.1?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* **Composite insert:** Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – Csn-AcdS-Histag – B0015, \[1863 bp]
* **Level 1 vector:** pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* **Template:** synthesized fragments assembled together
* **Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification):** 60 °C
* **Assembly method (Level 1):** Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* **Thermal cycle:**

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesized fragment using primers Csn F and ACCD R. Each primer carries a 5′ ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for level 0 vector entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the Csn start codon) at the 5′ end and TGTC at the 3′ end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pGEM-T Easy and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), Csn-AcdS-Histag ([BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                                    |
| Csn F          | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA AAA TCA GTA TGC AAA AAG CA |
| ACCD R         | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCT TAA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA T  |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                                             |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with Csn F and ACCD R primers flanking the CDS insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[1145 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

***Figure 1.*** **Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-AcdS-Histag-B0015.** 1 of 1 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[7767 bp]).

***Figure 2.*** **Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

sections.title: Application
sections.original:
### **Application**

This construct is the constitutive counterpart of the Light Responsive Expression Module in ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag. It gives the maximal output of the same cassette, which the light-controlled version can be compared against. It was run in our bioreactor to monitor production and secretion, and its protein can be applied to plants for functional testing.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.original:
**What the data mean.** ACCD is expressed in *B. subtilis* and secreted into the culture medium, so the construct works under optimal, constitutive conditions. Yield in the bioreactor was low, so there is room to improve it.

**Limitations.** Western blots show presence and size, not enzymatic activity, and activity assays are still planned. Pveg, EEBD-RBS0, and B0015 are reused across modules, which creates a risk of homologous recombination in the full circuit.

**Future directions.** We plan to improve yield through promoter strength and codon optimization, measure ACC deaminase activity directly, and compare Csn with SamyQ.

BBa_26D5AX7S.description: This **Protectant Module** constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS, and terminator B0015. The CDS of this construct encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) fused to the SamyQ signal peptide and a 6x Histag (SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag: [BBa\_26J0GJGZ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26j0gjgz)).

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) (LEA: [BBa\_26LTB0W1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1)) from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup.

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       Pveg (BBa\_K143012): a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction.

·       EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)): a composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*.

·       SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26J0GJGZ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26j0gjgz)): a translational fusion of three elements:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **LEA14 2.1 (**[<u>BBa\_26IN6G1D</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26in6g1d)**):** This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) from [<u>*Arabidopsis thaliana*</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O03983/entry) with its native start codon and stop codon removed. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from LEA14 wild-type ([<u>BBa\_26LTB0W1</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon. This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of LEA14
* **Potential application:** Protecting cellular structures and maintaining cellular stability under environmental stress conditions.

## Literature

**Rationale.** LEA proteins are small, partially folded, hydrophilic proteins that stabilise membranes and isolate ions to prevent water loss, and they keep other proteins from aggregating when water is withdrawn (Goyal et al., 2005; Hundertmark et al., 2008; Mertens et al., 2018). LEA14 from *Arabidopsis thaliana* is an intrinsically disordered protein of this family (Singh et al., 2005), and its overexpression raises salt-stress tolerance in *A. thaliana* (Jia et al., 2014). We selected it as a protectant cargo on the expectation that a secreted copy can help stabilise plant cell membranes under drought, salinity, heat and osmotic stress. This cassette carries the wild-type LEA14 coding sequence behind the Csn signal peptide, which exports the protein from the cell, and a C-terminal 6x Histag for detection and purification.

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression at a fixed level, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *Escherichia coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## References

1\. Goyal, K., Walton, L. J., & Tunnacliffe, A. (2005). LEA proteins prevent protein aggregation due to water stress. Biochemical Journal, 388(1), 151–157. [https://doi.org/10.1042/bj20041931](https://doi.org/10.1042/bj20041931)

2\. Hundertmark, M., Hincha, D. K., & Thalhammer, A. (2008). LEA (late embryogenesis abundant) proteins and their encoding genes in *Arabidopsis thaliana*. BMC Genomics, 9, Article 118. [https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-9-118](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-9-118)

3\. Jia, F., Qi, S., Li, H., Liu, P., Li, P., Wu, C., Zheng, C., & Huang, J. (2014). Overexpression of late embryogenesis abundant 14 enhances *Arabidopsis* salt stress tolerance. Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications, 454(4), 505–511. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2014.10.136](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2014.10.136)

4\. Mertens, J., Aliyu, H., & Cowan, D. A. (2018). LEA proteins and the evolution of the WHy domain. Applied and Environmental Microbiology, 84(15), Article e00539-18. [https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.00539-18](https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.00539-18)

5\. Singh, S., Cornilescu, C. C., Tyler, R. C., Cornilescu, G., Tonelli, M., Lee, M. S., & Markley, J. L. (2005). ## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* Composite insert: Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag – B0015, \[1287 bp]
* Level 1 vector: pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* Template: synthesized fragments assembled together
* Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification): 60 °C
* Assembly method (Level 1): Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* Thermal cycle:

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesized fragment using primers SamyQ F and ACCD R. Each primer carries a 5′ ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for level 0 vector entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the SamyQ start codon) at the 5′ end and TGTC at the 3′ end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pSTK-0C-sfGFP and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26J0GJGZ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26j0gjgz)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                                        |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                                   |
| SamyQ F        | ATATAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA TTC AAA AAC GAA AGC GGA C  |
| LEA R          | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCT TAA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA T |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                                            |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with pSTK-EXP-seq F and pSTK-EXP-seq R backbone primers, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[1423 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/a381f6ca-1228-4197-882d-fff4e1e9451b/ebfd0c76c34d04f11956d58605357d68079855d15bd02b40b5224ffebfa2c34a.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag-B0015.** 2 of 7 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1423 bp]).

**Figure 2. Clone \[X] was sequence-verified and used downstream.**
