BBa_26DE5E2Q.description: This module includes the light-responsive promoter P*cpcG2*-veg, the RBS EEBD-RBS0, a protectant CDS, and the terminator B0015, which together drive the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in *Bacillus Subtilis* after [BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10), [BBa\_261XH2RS](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs), and [BBa\_26BDO8AQ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq). The CDS evaluated was ACC deaminase protein, fused to the SamyQ secretion signal and 6x Histag. Together, these components convert light-induced regulatory signals into measurable visual outputs or stress-mitigation functions.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

The Light-Responsive Expression Module drives the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in Bacillus subtilis.

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       PcpcG2-veg (BBa\_254UKC9E): the light-responsive output promoter of the CcaSR system, activated by phosphorylated CcaR. It is a *B. subtilis*-adapted chimera of the cyanobacterial PcpcG2 promoter, engineered by Castillo-Hair et al. (2019).

·       EEBD-RBS0 (BBa\_26V6CPEV): a composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*.

·       SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26TOGLX3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3)): a translational fusion of an N-terminal Sec-dependent signal peptide, the ACC deaminase coding sequence with its native start and stop codons removed, and a 6x Histag fused at the C terminus followed by a stop codon, which allows protein detection and purification. The signal peptide and the *acdS* variant differ between the two versions of the module, as set out below.

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Green light-responsive expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis*.
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress on demand, as the output component of a stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor for plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**How PcpcG2-veg was engineered:** The output promoter was adapted to *B. subtilis* in stages by Castillo-Hair et al. (2019). The starting point was PcpcG2-172, the *E. coli*-optimised truncation of Schmidl et al. (2014), which removes an unwanted transcriptional start site. In *B. subtilis* it was weak. Swapping the original -10 hexamer for the *B. subtilis* consensus sequence, to improve σA RNA polymerase recruitment, gave PcpcG2-hy and about three times more output. Replacing the proximal region, meaning the sequence following the -10 hexamer, with that of the strong constitutive promoters PrpsD and Pveg gave the chimeras PcpcG2-rpsD and PcpcG2-veg; those two swaps are reported as increasing output transcription by 22- and 44-fold, and PcpcG2-veg was selected for its superior activity.

The values below are from Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), measured in *B. subtilis* PY79 by calibrated flow cytometry with an sfGFP reporter. They are not our measurements.

| Output promoter | Induced output (MEFL) | Uninduced output (MEFL) |
| --------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| PcpcG2-172      | 555 ± 65              | not reported            |
| PcpcG2-hy       | 1470 ± 110            | not reported            |
| PcpcG2-rpsD     | 32,400 ± 2800         | 174 ± 23                |
| PcpcG2-veg      | 64,000 ± 7600         | 378 ± 38                |

 

Two limits of that engineering matter for reading the part. The -35 box was left untouched, and only the -10 hexamer and the proximal region downstream of it were changed, because the CcaR operator region had to be kept intact. We chose PcpcG2-veg as the output promoter for the same reason it was selected in the published work, its higher output.

**Why the blocking device is on this module:** EEBD sits on this module and is absent from the light-sensing and transduction modules, because of the cargo. ACC deaminase is a secreted enzyme carried on a Sec signal peptide, and expression during cloning in *E. coli* risks unwanted protein production and loss of the construct. CcaS and CcaR, by contrast, have nothing to act on in *E. coli*, which has neither PCB nor a PcpcG2 promoter. Placing the terminator-between-recombination-sites device in front of the protectant CDS keeps the cassette silent through the *E. coli* cloning steps, and the same EEBD-RBS0 part supplies the RBS for the protectant CDS.

**What AcdS does:** ACC deaminase hydrolyses 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate, the precursor of the plant stress hormone ethylene, and so lowers the ethylene levels that inhibit plant growth under stress (Glick et al., 1998; Shah et al., 1998). The coding sequence is that of *Pseudomonas putida* strain UW4, taken from UniProt Q5PWZ8. The recombinant enzyme from that strain is 41 kDa and is selective and highly active towards ACC, with K(M) \= 3.4 ± 0.2 mM and k(cat) \= 146 ± 5 min⁻¹ at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0, declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5, tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and is lost above pH 10 (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

**The constitutive counterpart:** The constitutive Pveg versions of this cassette exist so that maximal secretion and production can be measured without the light switch, which gives the light-controlled module something to be compared against. A Western blot of the constitutive Csn-AcdS construct gave a band at about 37 kDa in the culture supernatant, consistent with the predicted size of the secreted enzyme. The 41 kDa quoted above is the purified recombinant enzyme of Hontzeas et al. (2004), which carries neither a cleaved signal peptide nor a His tag, and we have not compared the two forms directly. The equivalent characterisation of the light-responsive versions is not yet complete.

## References

2\. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Voigt, C. A. (2019). Optogenetic control of *Bacillus subtilis* gene expression. *Nature Communications, 10*, Article 3099. [https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6)

3\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). Expression and characterization of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase from the rhizobacterium *Pseudomonas putida* UW4: A key enzyme in bacterial plant growth promotion. *Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, 1703*(1), 11–19. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

4\. Shah, S., Li, J., Moffatt, B. A., & Glick, B. R. (1998). Isolation and characterization of ACC deaminase genes from two different plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. *Canadian Journal of Microbiology, 44*(9), 833–843. [https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074](https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074)

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The protectant coding sequence was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesised fragment, using primers SamyQ F and ACCD R for the SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag version. Each primer carries a 5' ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for Level 0 entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the start codon) at the 5' end and TGTC at the 3' end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pSTK-0C-sfGFP and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts PcpcG2-veg (BBa\_254UKC9E), EEBD-RBS0 (BBa\_26V6CPEV), the protectant CDS fusion ([BBa\_26TOGLX3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-1D-sfGFP Level 1 cloning vector (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica).*

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       Pveg (BBa\_K143012): a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction.

·       EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)): a composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*.

·       SamyQ-BoPep4-Histag ([BBa\_26ILD3SO](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ild3so))

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete cassette was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of BoPep4
* **Potential application:** Enhancing plant salt-stress tolerance as a component of plant-protecting bioprotectants

## Literature

**Rationale.** BoPep4 is a 23-residue mature plant elicitor peptide from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea* var. *italica*), sequence GILIGSKKRPREPHSSGKPGGHN. It works through auxin and abscisic acid signalling crosstalk to raise salt-stress tolerance in broccoli, lowering the Na⁺/K⁺ ratio and promoting leaf wax and cutin accumulation (Wang, A., et al., 2022). The peptide is 23 residues, short enough that it cannot be detected without the tag. This cassette carries the wild-type BoPep4 coding sequence behind the SamyQ signal peptide, which directs it into the Sec-dependent secretion pathway. The 6x Histag is fused N-terminally to the peptide, which allows detection and quantification of the short peptide.

**Why the wild-type coding sequence.** Wild-type BoPep4 was the weakest starting point of our whole construct series for predicted translation initiation. Start+15 accessibility was 0.396 and Shine-Dalgarno core accessibility 0.067, both below the roughly 0.50 usability threshold we worked to and below the Ho1 reference baseline of 0.681. We kept an untouched copy in the set as the baseline for the BoPep4 variants, both the two recoded versions and the mutant and truncated peptides. Our BoPep4 cassettes, this one and the ones carrying BoPep4 2.1 and BoPep4 2.2, all use the SamyQ signal peptide and differ only in the first 15 codons of the coding sequence. They are the one place in our part set where the effect of 5′ recoding can be read on its own, with everything else held fixed.

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression at a fixed level, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *Escherichia coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## References

1\. Wang, A., Guo, J., Wang, S., Zhang, Y., Lu, F., Duan, J., Liu, Z., & Ji, W. (2022). BoPEP4, a C-terminally encoded plant elicitor peptide from broccoli, plays a role in salinity stress tolerance. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 23(6), Article 3090. [https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090)

2\. Caro-Astorga, J., Rogan, M., Malcı, K., Ming, H., Debenedictis, E., James, P., & Ellis, T. (2025). SubtiToolKit: A bioengineering kit for *Bacillus subtilis* and Gram-positive bacteria. Trends in Biotechnology, 43(6), 1446–1469. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004)

sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

This cassette was built differently from the others. The whole construct was obtained by de novo gene synthesis, so there is no Level 0 entry-cloning step and no amplification of the coding-sequence fusion for it.

* Composite insert: Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – SamyQ-BoPep4-Histag – B0015, \[910 bp]
* Level 1 vector: pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* Template: de novo synthesised cassette
* Level 0 entry step: none 
* Assembly method (Level 1): Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2 enzyme
* Thermal cycle:

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

*

The coding sequence was incorporated into Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-BoPep4-B0015 by de novo gene synthesis. Our six other constitutive protectant cassettes were assembled from separate Level 0 parts in a Golden Gate reaction with BsaI-HFv2, and that narrative does not apply here. The construct was assembled into pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP. The amplification primers used on the other cassettes, SamyQ F and BoPep R, were not needed for this one. 

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with SamyQ F and pSTK-EXP-seq R primers, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

## Results

Although the gel image for Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-Bopep4-Histag-B0015 is unavailable, the construct was successfully assembled and verified by gel electrophoresis.

**Figure 1. Sequencing of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-BoPep4-Histag-B0015.**

·       SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag ([BBa\_267B69E3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-267b69e3)): The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (BBa\_K1074014):** N-terminal signal peptide of the amyQ gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in Bacillus subtilis (and related lineages like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **BoPep4 2.2 (**[<u>**BBa\_26ERHWWI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26erhwwi) **):** encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica),* with its native start codon removed, followed by a stop codon. ·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of BoPep4
* **Potential application:** Enhancing plant salt-stress tolerance as a component of plant-protecting bioprotectants

## Literature

**Rationale.** BoPep4 is a 23-residue mature plant elicitor peptide from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea* var. *italica*), sequence GILIGSKKRPREPHSSGKPGGHN. It works through auxin and abscisic acid signalling crosstalk to raise salt-stress tolerance in broccoli, lowering the Na⁺/K⁺ ratio and promoting leaf wax and cutin accumulation (Wang, A., et al., 2022). This cassette carries the recoded BoPep4 2.1 coding sequence behind the SamyQ signal peptide, which directs the peptide into the Sec-dependent secretion pathway. The 6x Histag is fused N-terminally to the peptide, which allows detection and quantification of the short peptide.

**Why the recoded 5′ end.**The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and the start codon influences translation initiation in bacteria, independently of the encoded protein sequence. Following Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), our design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 coding sequence as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 (Lorenz et al., 2011) generated and folded tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5′ window (residual recombination site, MF001 RBS, spacer, SamyQ ORF and the first 90 nt of the CDS), scoring the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG) and combining the two into a balance score. Wild-type BoPep4 was the weakest starting point of the whole construct series, with start+15 accessibility 0.396 and Shine-Dalgarno core accessibility 0.067. BoPep4 2.2 is the second recoding solution we took forward from that run, alongside BoPep4 2.1. Eight of the first 15 BoPep4 codons were changed (c1 GGC→GGT, c2 ATT→ATA, c3 TTA→CTC, c5 GGA→GGT, c6 TCA→AGT, c9 AGA→CGG, c11 AGA→CGG, c15 TCA→AGT), and the peptide sequence is unchanged from wild type. Predicted start+15 accessibility rose from 0.396 to 0.432 and Shine-Dalgarno core accessibility from 0.067 to 0.658, giving a combined balance score of 1.090. The codon adaptation index against *B. subtilis* 168 usage (Kazusa DNA Research Institute, n.d.) dropped from 0.87 to 0.77. These scores are predictions. Translation initiation from this cassette has not been measured.

**Why 2.2 as well as 2.1.** The two solutions divide the gain differently. BoPep4 2.1 changed nine codons and reached start+15 0.497 with a Shine-Dalgarno core of 0.634, for a balance of 1.131; BoPep4 2.2 changed eight codons and reached start+15 0.432 with a Shine-Dalgarno core of 0.658, for a balance of 1.090. BoPep4 2.2 therefore gains more access at the Shine-Dalgarno core and less at the start codon, and we carry both so that the two can be compared at the bench.

**Why three BoPep4 versions.** Our three BoPep4 cassettes, carrying wild-type BoPep4, BoPep4 2.1 and BoPep4 2.2, all use the SamyQ signal peptide and differ only in the first 15 codons. They are the one place in our part set where the effect of 5′ recoding can be read on its own, with everything else held fixed.

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression at a fixed level, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *Escherichia coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

1\. Wang, A., Guo, J., Wang, S., Zhang, Y., Lu, F., Duan, J., Liu, Z., & Ji, W. (2022). BoPEP4, a C-terminally encoded plant elicitor peptide from broccoli, plays a role in salinity stress tolerance. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 23(6), Article 3090. [https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090)

2\. Caro-Astorga, J., Rogan, M., Malcı, K., Ming, H., Debenedictis, E., James, P., & Ellis, T. (2025). SubtiToolKit: A bioengineering kit for *Bacillus subtilis* and Gram-positive bacteria. Trends in Biotechnology, 43(6), 1446–1469. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004)

sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* **Composite insert:** Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag – B0015, \[906 bp]
* **Level 1 vector:** pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* **Template:** synthesized fragments assembled together
* **Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification):** 60 °C
* **Assembly method (Level 1):** Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* **Thermal cycle:**

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was cloned into pSTK-0C-sfGFP and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), SamyQ-BoPep 2.2-Histag ([BBa\_267B69E3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-267b69e3)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                                |
| SamyQ F        | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGATTC AAAAACGAAAGCGGAC             |
| BoPep R        | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA TG |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                                         |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with backbone primers primers flanking the CDS insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[678 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/e8fee956-00f9-4129-92e7-4ee7882e2bd5/7ae42b9bff17d0d916103775d7a1c7529452c0fb34b08ae881e2f5d1dfc68cc9.avif)

***Figure 1.*** **Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag-B0015.** 4 of 5 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[678 bp]).

***Figure 2.*** **Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

BBa_26ILD3SO.title: SamyQ-BoPep4-Histag
BBa_26ILD3SO.description: This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica).* BoPep4 acts as a peptide hormone and signaling molecule to regulate plant defense mechanisms and salt tolerance. The BoPep4 ([BBa\_265CD14Z](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265cd14z)) protein is fused to the alpha-amylase signal peptide (SamyQ) at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus. The BoPep4 coding sequence was codon-optimized for *B. subtilis.*

BBa_26IN6G1D.title: LEA14 2.1
BBa_26IN6G1D.description: This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup; the wild-type LEA sequence is registered as [BBa\_26LTB0W1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1). The paper showed overexpression of AtLEA14 enhances salt stress tolerance in *Arabidopsis thaliana*. Therefore, LEA14 is might be the potential gene involved in plant responses to abiotic stress.  In this variant, the first 15 amino acids of the LEA14 coding sequence were codon-optimized, which is predicted to reduce mRNA secondary structure at the 5′ end and thereby enhance translation initiation.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## **About**

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 
*  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 

## **Literature**

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

BBa_26J0GJGZ.description: This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup*;* the wild-type LEA sequence is registered as [BBa\_26LTB0W1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1). The paper showed overexpression of AtLEA14 enhances salt stress tolerance in *Arabidopsis thaliana*. Therefore, LEA14 is might be the potential gene involved in plant responses to abiotic stress. sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14)from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup. 

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **LEA14 2.1 (**[<u>BBa\_26IN6G1D</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26in6g1d)**):** This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) from [<u>*Arabidopsis thaliana*</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O03983/entry) with its native start codon and stop codon removed. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from LEA14 wild-type ([<u>BBa\_26LTB0W1</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon. This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of LEA 14 in the host *B. subtilis*
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants

## Dry lab / computational analysis

The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and start codon heavily influences the translation-initiation efficiency inside bacteria. Synonymous codons, meaning codons that result in the same amino acids, in the 5’ end of a CDS can impact how the mRNA folds near the binding site. The folding can either hide or expose the Shine Dalgarno sequence and start codon, impacting the efficiency of ribosome binding and translation initiation. Following this concept suggested by Castillo-Hair (2019), the design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the LEA14 CDS as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 was used to generate and fold tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5’ window (residual recombination site + MF001 RBS + spacer + SamyQ ORF + first 90 nt of cds), determining the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG) and creating a balance score. 

SamyQ-LEA 2.1-Histag was determined to be the best candidate from the run: 6 of the first 15 LEA14 codons were changed (c1 GCG→GCA, c2 TCT→AGT, c3 TTA→CTC, c4 TTA→CTC, c10 TTT→TTC, c11 GTA→GTC). The predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.538 to 0.669 and SD-core accessibility decreased from 0.357 to 0.307 when compared to the wild type, resulting in an overall balance score gain of 0.895 to 0.976. The codon adaptation index against B. subtilis 168 usage dropped from 0.85 to 0.81. Instead of following Castillo’s rule, which prioritizes low GC content and A over U, the program individually folded and verified every candidate to verify improved accessibility, as the Castillo-rule-applied control produced a start+15 score of only 0.669 and an SD-core score of 0.078 (balance 0.748), which was lower than wild type.

## References

1. Goyal, K., Walton, L. J., & Tunnacliffe, A. (2005). LEA proteins prevent protein aggregation due to water stress. *Biochemical Journal, 388(1)*, 151–157. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1042/bj20041931</u>](https://doi.org/10.1042/bj20041931)  
2. Hundertmark, M., Hincha, D. K., & Thalhammer, A. (2008). LEA (late embryogenesis abundant) proteins and their encoding genes in *Arabidopsis thaliana*. *BMC Genomics, 9*, Article 118. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-9-118</u>](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-9-118)  
3. Jia, F., Qi, S., Li, H., Liu, P., Li, P., Wu, C., Zheng, C., & Huang, J. (2014). Overexpression of late embryogenesis abundant 14 enhances *Arabidopsis* salt stress tolerance. *Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications, 454(4)*, 505–511. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2014.10.136</u>](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2014.10.136)  
4. Mertens, J., Aliyu, H., & Cowan, D. A. (2018). LEA proteins and the evolution of the WHy domain. *Applied and Environmental Microbiology, 84(15)*, Article e00539-18. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.00539-18</u>](https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.00539-18)  
5. Singh, S., Cornilescu, C. C., Tyler, R. C., Cornilescu, G., Tonelli, M., Lee, M. S., & Markley, J. L. (2005). Solution structure of a late embryogenesis abundant protein (LEA14) from *Arabidopsis thaliana*, a cellular stress-related protein. *Protein Science, 14(10)*, 2601–2609. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1110/ps.051579205</u>](https://doi.org/10.1110/ps.051579205)

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

Construct details:

* **Insert:** SamyQ signal peptide – LEA14 2.1 – 6x Histag, \[561 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                                        |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SamyQ F     | ATATAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA TTC AAA AAC GAA AGC GGA C  |
| LEA14 R     | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCT TAA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA T |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetic fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the SamyQ and STK R primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag insert \[561 bp] plus the vector sequence between the His Tag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[770 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, LEA14 2.1 coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## Result

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/da1b3de3-ebd2-4a73-bb4e-2ef6dc8e8ec8/2463682d514cfc7eaa3e7c9162c24cb2fde222c8a612aefb787f00e93d58e3a9.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-0C-SamyQ-LEA14 2.1-Histag**. The figure indicates that 2 of 2 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[770 bp])

**Figure 2. Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

BBa_26MA70QI.title: AcdS
BBa_26MA70QI.description: This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4. It is an enzyme commonly found in plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of the plant hormone ethylene, thereby alleviating ethylene-induced growth inhibition in plants under stress. The ACC deaminase coding sequence was codon-optimized for *B. subtilis*.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]

## Literature

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS: [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **Csn signal peptide:** the N-terminal Sec-dependent signal peptide of *B. subtilis* chitosanase (gene *csn*), which directs the protein to the secretion pathway and is cleaved off during export. Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **AcdS (**[<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida* *(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303), with its native start codon and stop codon removed  
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis. 

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis*
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants

## Literature

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10.

Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **AcdS (**[<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida* *(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303), with its native start codon and stop codon removed  
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis. 

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* WB800
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis*
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants

## Literature

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10.

## Construction/assembly (wetlab)

To improve the reliability of our Level 0 entry step, the Csn-AcdS-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pGEM-T Easy vector, giving pGEM-T Easy-Csn-AcdS. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the Csn-AcdS-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

* **Construct details:**
* **Insert:** Csn signal peptide – AcdS – 6x Histag, \[1122 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                                         |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Csn F       | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA AAA TCA GTA TGC AAA AAG CA |
| ACCD R      | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCT TAA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA T  |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetized fragment
* **Vector:** pGEM-T Easy (ampicillin resistance, blue/white screening)

## Verification (wetlab)

Colonies from the pGEM-T Easy-Csn:ACCD transformation were screened by colony PCR with the T7 and SP6 primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the Csn-AcdS-Histag insert \[1122 bp] plus the vector sequence between the T7 and SP6 priming sites, for a total of \[1372 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, AcdS coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## **Results**

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/2e0c7969-989e-4d77-8537-5ad723e0e269/54aa2f3c3988069d3a6b4b20e1990c3faf3ab9d4bb5bbc882c5adef17adcce74.avif)

**Figure 1.** **Colony PCR of pGEM-T Easy-Csn-AcdS-Histag.** The figure indicates that 2 of 4 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1372 bp])

**Figure 2. Clone 3 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-AcdS-Histag-B0015** ([BBa\_26CXI09X](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26cxi09x)): this **Protectant Module** constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS, and terminator B0015.
* **PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-AcdS-Histag-B0015** ([BBa\_26Q3LKZU](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q3lkzu)): this module includes the light-responsive promoter P*cpcG2*-veg, the RBS EEBD-RBS0, a protectant CDS, and the terminator B0015, which together drive the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in *Bacillus Subtilis* after [BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10), [BBa\_261XH2RS](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs), and [BBa\_26BDO8AQ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq).
* **ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag** ([BBa\_2654HAF3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2654haf3)): the system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica).*

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (BBa\_K1074014):** N-terminal signal peptide of the amyQ gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in Bacillus subtilis (and related lineages like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **BoPep4 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_26LYCBW0**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26lycbw0)**):** encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica),* with its native start codon removed, followed by a stop codon. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** fused N-terminally to the peptide. This allows detection and quantification of the short peptide after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety Level:** S1
* **Target organism:** Bacillus subtilis \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of BoPep4 in the host B. subtilis
* **Potential application:** Enhancing plant salt-stress tolerance as a component of plant-protecting bioprotectants

## Dry lab / computational analysis

The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and start codon influences translation-initiation efficiency inside bacteria, independent of the encoded protein sequence. Following the concept suggested by Castillo-Hair (2019), the design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 CDS as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 was used to generate and fold tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5′ window (residual recombination site + MF001 RBS + spacer + SamyQ ORF + first 90 nt of CDS), determining the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG), and combining these into a balance score.

Wild-type BoPep4 was the weakest starting point of the whole construct series: start+15 accessibility was only 0.396 and SD-core accessibility only 0.067, both below the \~0.50 usability threshold and the Ho1 reference baseline (0.681). SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag was determined to be the best candidate from the run: 9 of the first 15 BoPep4 codons were changed (c2 ATT→ATC, c5 GGA→GGT, c6 TCA→AGT, c7 AAA→AAG, c10 CCG→CCT, c11 AGA→AGG, c13 CCG→CCT, c14 CAT→CAC, c15 TCA→TCC). The predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.396 to 0.497, and SD-core accessibility rose sharply from 0.067 to 0.634 (roughly a 9.5-fold gain), resulting in an overall balance score gain of 0.462 to 1.131. The codon adaptation index in B. subtilis 168 dropped from 0.87 to 0.77. We verified this variant against a Castillo-rule-applied control (low GC content, A over U): the control reached a start+15 of 0.677 and an SD-core of 0.425 (balance 1.102) an improvement over wild type, but still below the balance achieved by individually folding and verifying each candidate.

## References

1. Wang, A., Guo, J., Wang, S., Zhang, Y., Lu, F., Duan, J., Liu, Z., & Ji, W. (2022). BoPEP4, a C-Terminally Encoded Plant Elicitor Peptide from Broccoli, Plays a Role in Salinity Stress Tolerance. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 23(6), 3090–3090. [<u>https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090</u>](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23063090)
2. Li, R., Liu, M., Hu, X., Li, J., Pang, Q., Yan, X., Li, J., & Ji, W. (2026). Broccoli plant elicitor peptide BoPep4 enhances plant salt tolerance by improving glucosinolate metabolism. Plant Science, 364, 112954.

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The SamyQ-Bopep4 2.1-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-SamyQ-Bopep4 2.1-Histag. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the SamyQ-Bopep4 2.1-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

Construct details:

* **Insert:** SamyQ signal peptide – Bopep4 2.1 – 6x Histag, \[177 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SamyQ F     | ATATAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA TTC AAA AAC GAA AGC GGA C |
| BoPep R     | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA TG   |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetic fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the SamyQ and STK R primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag insert \[177 bp] plus the vector sequence between the Histag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[536 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, BoPep4 2.1 coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/603279c2-8482-45a5-9c9a-d23fd0bfc8dd/8834ba1b94f0d101c311b9adae10aa4cea38616e5f61a5f90a8e5450d5de15d1.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-0C-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.1-Histag**. The figure indicates that 18 of 19 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[536 bp])

**Figure 2. Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

The Light-Responsive Expression Module drives the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in Bacillus subtilis. 

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       PcpcG2-veg (BBa\_254UKC9E): the light-responsive output promoter of the CcaSR system, activated by phosphorylated CcaR. It is a *B. subtilis*-adapted chimera of the cyanobacterial PcpcG2 promoter, engineered by Castillo-Hair et al. (2019).

·       EEBD-RBS0 (BBa\_26V6CPEV): a composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*.

·       Csn-AcdS-Histag ([BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)): a translational fusion of an N-terminal Sec-dependent signal peptide, the ACC deaminase coding sequence with its native start and stop codons removed, and a 6x Histag fused at the C terminus followed by a stop codon, which allows protein detection and purification. The signal peptide and the *acdS* variant differ between the two versions of the module, as set out below.

·       B0015 (BBa\_B0015): a high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Green light-responsive expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis*.
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress on demand, as the output component of a stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor for plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**How PcpcG2-veg was engineered:** The output promoter was adapted to *B. subtilis* in stages by Castillo-Hair et al. (2019). The starting point was PcpcG2-172, the *E. coli*-optimised truncation of Schmidl et al. (2014), which removes an unwanted transcriptional start site. In *B. subtilis* it was weak. Swapping the original -10 hexamer for the *B. subtilis* consensus sequence, to improve σA RNA polymerase recruitment, gave PcpcG2-hy and about three times more output. Replacing the proximal region, meaning the sequence following the -10 hexamer, with that of the strong constitutive promoters PrpsD and Pveg gave the chimeras PcpcG2-rpsD and PcpcG2-veg; those two swaps are reported as increasing output transcription by 22- and 44-fold, and PcpcG2-veg was selected for its superior activity.

The values below are from Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), measured in *B. subtilis* PY79 by calibrated flow cytometry with an sfGFP reporter. They are not our measurements.

| Output promoter | Induced output (MEFL) | Uninduced output (MEFL) |
| --------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| PcpcG2-172      | 555 ± 65              | not reported            |
| PcpcG2-hy       | 1470 ± 110            | not reported            |
| PcpcG2-rpsD     | 32,400 ± 2800         | 174 ± 23                |
| PcpcG2-veg      | 64,000 ± 7600         | 378 ± 38                |

 

Two limits of that engineering matter for reading the part. The -35 box was left untouched, and only the -10 hexamer and the proximal region downstream of it were changed, because the CcaR operator region had to be kept intact. We chose PcpcG2-veg as the output promoter for the same reason it was selected in the published work, its higher output.

**Why the blocking device is on this module:** EEBD sits on this module and is absent from the light-sensing and transduction modules, because of the cargo. ACC deaminase is a secreted enzyme carried on a Sec signal peptide, and expression during cloning in *E. coli* risks unwanted protein production and loss of the construct. CcaS and CcaR, by contrast, have nothing to act on in *E. coli*, which has neither PCB nor a PcpcG2 promoter. Placing the terminator-between-recombination-sites device in front of the protectant CDS keeps the cassette silent through the *E. coli* cloning steps, and the same EEBD-RBS0 part supplies the RBS for the protectant CDS.

**What AcdS does:** ACC deaminase hydrolyses 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate, the precursor of the plant stress hormone ethylene, and so lowers the ethylene levels that inhibit plant growth under stress (Glick et al., 1998; Shah et al., 1998). The coding sequence is that of *Pseudomonas putida* strain UW4, taken from UniProt Q5PWZ8. The recombinant enzyme from that strain is 41 kDa and is selective and highly active towards ACC, with K(M) \= 3.4 ± 0.2 mM and k(cat) \= 146 ± 5 min⁻¹ at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0, declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5, tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and is lost above pH 10 (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

**The constitutive counterpart:** The constitutive Pveg versions of this cassette exist so that maximal secretion and production can be measured without the light switch, which gives the light-controlled module something to be compared against. A Western blot of the constitutive Csn-AcdS construct gave a band at about 37 kDa in the culture supernatant, consistent with the predicted size of the secreted enzyme. The 41 kDa quoted above is the purified recombinant enzyme of Hontzeas et al. (2004), which carries neither a cleaved signal peptide nor a His tag, and we have not compared the two forms directly. The equivalent characterisation of the light-responsive versions is not yet complete.

## References

2\. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Voigt, C. A. (2019). Optogenetic control of *Bacillus subtilis* gene expression. *Nature Communications, 10*, Article 3099. [https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6)

3\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The protectant coding sequence was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesised fragment, using primers Csn F and ACCD R for the Csn-AcdS-Histag version. Each primer carries a 5' ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for Level 0 entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the start codon) at the 5' end and TGTC at the 3' end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pGEM-T Easy and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts PcpcG2-veg (BBa\_254UKC9E), EEBD-RBS0 (BBa\_26V6CPEV), the protectant CDS fusion ([BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-1D-sfGFP Level 1 cloning vector (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

**CONSTRUCT DETAILS**

*  Composite insert: PcpcG2-veg – EEBD-RBS0 – Csn-AcdS-Histag – B0015, \[1788 bp]
* Level 1 vector: pSTK-1D-sfGFP (Level 1 cloning vector), \[ampicillin]
* Template: synthesised fragments assembled together
* Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification): 60 °C
* Assembly method: Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* Thermal cycle:

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-1D-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with backbone primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the insert plus the vector sequence between the priming sites, for a total of \[1588 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, blocking device, RBS, protectant CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 2 optogenetic system constructed in the pSTK-EXP2 vector.

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5' to 3')                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Csn F       | ATATATGAAG ACATCTGAGG TCTCATATGA AAATCAGTAT GCAAAAAGCA |
| ACCD R      | ATATATGAAG ACATGAGGGG TCTCATGTCT TAATGATGAT GATGATGAT  |
| pSTK-seq F  | agtgccacctgacgtctaagaaacc                              |
| pSTK-seq R  | tctttcctgcgttatcccctgattc                              |

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/f53874a3-c117-479a-94b4-16cd4d3744ca/007541e6fe2482f0a198c05fc9ab94e27b40cc3d2d2a5aec295852f946cf741c.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-1D-PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-AcdS-Histag-B0015.** 2 of 6 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1588 bp]).

Figure 2. Clone \[X] of each version was sequence-verified and used for downstream experiments.

## Overview

This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) (LEA: [BBa\_26LTB0W1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1)) from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup.

The part is a composite transcription unit with four elements, in this order:

·       Pveg (BBa\_K143012): a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction.

·       EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)): a composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*.

·       Csn-LEA14-Histag ([BBa\_26ZQ1T72](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zq1t72)): a translational fusion of three elements:

1. **Csn signal peptide:** the N-terminal Sec-dependent signal peptide of *B. subtilis* chitosanase (gene *csn*), which directs the protein to the secretion pathway and is cleaved off during export. ## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of LEA14
* **Potential application:** Protecting cellular structures and maintaining cellular stability under environmental stress conditions.

## Literature

**Rationale.** LEA proteins are small, partially folded, hydrophilic proteins that stabilise membranes and isolate ions to prevent water loss, and they keep other proteins from aggregating when water is withdrawn (Goyal et al., 2005; Hundertmark et al., 2008; Mertens et al., 2018). **Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression at a fixed level, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *Escherichia coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* Composite insert: Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – Csn-LEA14-Histag – B0015, \[1302 bp]
* Level 1 vector: pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* Template: synthesized fragments assembled together
* Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification): 60 °C
* Assembly method (Level 1): Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* Thermal cycle:

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesized fragment using primers Csn F and ACCD R. Each primer carries a 5′ ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for level 0 vector entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the Csn start codon) at the 5′ end and TGTC at the 3′ end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pGEM-T Easy and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), Csn-LEA14-Histag ([BBa\_26ZQ1T72](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zq1t72)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                                    |
| Csn F          | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATC TGA GGT CTC ATA TGA AAA TCA GTA TGC AAA AAG CA |
| LEA R          | ATA TAT GAA GAC ATG AGG GGT CTC ATG TCT TAA TGA TGA TGA TGA TGA T  |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                                             |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with Csn F and  pSTK-EXP-seq R primers, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[735 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/230c92c1-9633-4bc5-bcce-b77e115c013e/a2f980ff8969210f1161786da8f1adad96e9d7efeb22feeaa7d96a1e1d81fe23.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-LEA14-Histag-B0015.** 1 of 1 colony gave a band at the expected size (\[735 bp]).

**Figure 2. Clone \[X] was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

BBa_26TOGLX3.title: SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag
BBa_26TOGLX3.description: This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4*;* the wild-type acdS sequence is registered as [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi).  It is an enzyme commonly found in plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of the plant hormone ethylene, thereby alleviating ethylene-induced growth inhibition in plants under stress. The ACC deaminase protein is fused to the alpha-amylase signal peptide (SamyQ) at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS:[ <u>BBa\_26MA70QI</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **AcdS 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_262YYNPV**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-262yynpv)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida* *(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303) , with its native start codon and stop codon removed  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from AcdS wild-type ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis* 
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants

## Dry lab / computational analysis

The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and start codon heavily influences the translation-initiation efficiency inside bacteria. Synonymous codons, meaning codons that result in the same amino acids, in the 5' end of a CDS can impact how the mRNA folds near the binding site. The folding can either hide or expose the Shine Dalgarno sequence and start codon, impacting the efficiency of ribosome binding and translation initiation. Following this concept suggested by Castillo-Hair (2019), the design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the acdS CDS as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 was used to generate and fold tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5' window (residual recombination site + MF001 RBS + spacer + SamyQ ORF + first 90 nt of cds), determining the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG) and creating a balance score.

SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag was determined to be the best candidate from the run: 12 of the first 15 acdS codons were changed (c2 TTA→TTG, c3 AAT→AAC, c4 AGA→CGC, c7 AGA→CGC, c8 TAT→TAC, c9 CCG→CCC, c10 TTA→CTT, c11 ACA→ACT, c12 TTC→TTT, c13 GGA→GGG, c14 CCG→CCA, c15 AGC→AGT). The predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.563 to 0.773 and SD-core accessibility improved from 0.088 to 0.203 when compared to the wild type, resulting in an overall balance score gain of 0.651 to 0.976. The codon adaptation index against B. subtilis 168 usage dropped from 0.85 to 0.75. Instead of following Castillo's rule, which prioritizes low GC content and A over U, the program individually folded and verified every candidate to verify improved accessibility, as the Castillo-rule-applied control produced a start+15 score of only 0.698 and an SD-core score of 0.186 (balance 0.884), which, although still an improvement over wild type, remained lower than the balance achieved through individual verification of every candidate.

## Literature

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

## References

1\. UniProt Consortium. (n.d.). *Q5PWZ8*. UniProt. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from[<u>UniProt entry Q5PWZ8</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5PWZ8/entry?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

2\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). Expression and characterization of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase from the rhizobacterium pseudomonas putida UW4: A key enzyme in bacterial plant growth promotion. *Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, 1703(1)*, 11–19. PubMed.[<u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015</u>](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

3\. Shah, S., Li, J., Moffatt, B. A., & Glick, B. R. (1998). Isolation and characterization of ACC deaminase genes from two different plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. *Canadian Journal of Microbiology, 44*(9), 833–843.[<u>https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074</u>](https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074)

4\. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Voigt, C. A. (2019). Optogenetic control of Bacillus subtilis gene expression. Nature Communications, 10, Article 3099. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6</u>](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6) 

5\. Kazusa DNA Research Institute. (n.d.). Codon usage database: Bacillus subtilis subsp. subtilis str. 168 (taxid:1423). [<u>https://www.kazusa.or.jp/codon/</u>](https://www.kazusa.or.jp/codon/) 

6\. Glick, B. R., Penrose, D. M., & Li, J. (1998). A model for the lowering of plant ethylene concentrations by plant growth-promoting bacteria. *Journal of Theoretical Biology*, *190*(1), 63–68.[ <u>https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532</u>](https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532)
