## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS:[ <u>BBa\_26MA70QI</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **AcdS 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_262YYNPV**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-262yynpv)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida* *(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303) , with its native start codon and stop codon removed  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from AcdS wild-type ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* WB800 
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis* 
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants

## Dry lab / computational analysis

The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and start codon heavily influences the translation-initiation efficiency inside bacteria. Synonymous codons, meaning codons that result in the same amino acids, in the 5' end of a CDS can impact how the mRNA folds near the binding site. The folding can either hide or expose the Shine Dalgarno sequence and start codon, impacting the efficiency of ribosome binding and translation initiation. Following this concept suggested by Castillo-Hair (2019), the design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the acdS CDS as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 was used to generate and fold tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5' window (residual recombination site + MF001 RBS + spacer + SamyQ ORF + first 90 nt of cds), determining the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG) and creating a balance score.

SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag was determined to be the best candidate from the run: 12 of the first 15 acdS codons were changed (c2 TTA→TTG, c3 AAT→AAC, c4 AGA→CGC, c7 AGA→CGC, c8 TAT→TAC, c9 CCG→CCC, c10 TTA→CTT, c11 ACA→ACT, c12 TTC→TTT, c13 GGA→GGG, c14 CCG→CCA, c15 AGC→AGT). The predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.563 to 0.773 and SD-core accessibility improved from 0.088 to 0.203 when compared to the wild type, resulting in an overall balance score gain of 0.651 to 0.976. The codon adaptation index against B. subtilis 168 usage dropped from 0.85 to 0.75. Instead of following Castillo's rule, which prioritizes low GC content and A over U, the program individually folded and verified every candidate to verify improved accessibility, as the Castillo-rule-applied control produced a start+15 score of only 0.698 and an SD-core score of 0.186 (balance 0.884), which, although still an improvement over wild type, remained lower than the balance achieved through individual verification of every candidate.

## Literature

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

## References

1\. UniProt Consortium. (n.d.). *Q5PWZ8*. UniProt. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from[<u>UniProt entry Q5PWZ8</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5PWZ8/entry?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

2\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). Expression and characterization of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase from the rhizobacterium pseudomonas putida UW4: A key enzyme in bacterial plant growth promotion. *Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, 1703(1)*, 11–19. PubMed.[<u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015</u>](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

3\. Shah, S., Li, J., Moffatt, B. A., & Glick, B. R. (1998). Isolation and characterization of ACC deaminase genes from two different plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. *Canadian Journal of Microbiology, 44*(9), 833–843.[<u>https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074</u>](https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074)

4\. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Voigt, C. A. (2019). Optogenetic control of Bacillus subtilis gene expression. Nature Communications, 10, Article 3099. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6</u>](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6) 

5\. Kazusa DNA Research Institute. (n.d.). Codon usage database: Bacillus subtilis subsp. subtilis str. 168 (taxid:1423). [<u>https://www.kazusa.or.jp/codon/</u>](https://www.kazusa.or.jp/codon/) 

6\. Glick, B. R., Penrose, D. M., & Li, J. (1998). A model for the lowering of plant ethylene concentrations by plant growth-promoting bacteria. *Journal of Theoretical Biology*, *190*(1), 63–68.[ <u>https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532</u>](https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532)

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

* **Insert:** SamyQ signal peptide – AcdS 2.1 – 6x Histag, \[1122 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                         |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| SamyQ F     | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGA TTCAAAAACGAAAGCGGAC |
| ACCD R      | ATATATGAAGACATGAGGGGTCTCATG TCTTAATGATGATGATGATGAT |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetized fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the SamyQ and STK primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the SamyQ-AcdS-Histag insert \[1122 bp] plus the vector sequence between the Histag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[1331 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, AcdS coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/ac216f11-0619-4f9d-bde3-95eaddb96dac/0b523a149a6f3fe081a164343b3fcb40b83b8a65e393e3a440278ae7b424bccc.avif)

**Figure 1. Colony PCR of pSTK-0C-SamyQ-AcdS-Histag 2.1.** The figure indicates that 2 of 2 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1331 bp])

**Figure 2. Clone 2 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

sections.title: Application
sections.original:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26XVQ3FS**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xvq3fs)): this **Protectant Module** constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS, and terminator B0015.
* **PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26DE5E2Q**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26de5e2q)): this module includes the light-responsive promoter P*cpcG2*-veg, the RBS EEBD-RBS0, a protectant CDS, and the terminator B0015, which together drive the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in *Bacillus Subtilis* after[ <u>BBa\_26XZYM10</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10),[ <u>BBa\_261XH2RS</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs), and[ <u>BBa\_26BDO8AQ</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq).
* **ccaSR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag** ([<u>**BBa\_26U8UTMH**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26u8utmh)): the system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control.

BBa_26U8UTMH.title: ccaSR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag
BBa_26U8UTMH.description: The system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control. The PCB Production Module ([BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10)) supplies the chromophore phycocyanobilin. The Light Sensing Module ([BBa\_261XH2RS](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs)) expresses CcaS-m3, which detects green light and autophosphorylates. The Transduction Module ([BBa\_26BDO8AQ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq)) expresses CcaR, which receives its phosphoryl group. Phosphorylated CcaR activates PcpcG2-veg in the Light-Responsive Expression Module ([BBa\_26DE5E2Q](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26de5e2q)), driving secretion of ACC deaminase via the SamyQ signal peptide. Expression is on in green light and off in red, giving external control over protein production instead of a constant burden on the cell.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This is the assembled Level 2 construct of our stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor. It carries four Level 1 transcriptional units on a single plasmid, so that *Bacillus subtilis* can sense and respond to light signals on its own. The first module makes the chromophore PCB, the second expresses the sensor kinase CcaSm3, and the third expresses the response regulator CcaR. The fourth is the output, which secretes ACC deaminase (AcdS) when green light is present - specifically, CcasR-Csn-AcdS-Histag (Bba\_2654HAF3), the wildtype output with the Csn signal peptide.

The part is a composite of four transcriptional units in this order: 

1. PCB production ([BBa\_26XZYM10](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10)): PtagC + RBS ([<u>**BBa\_26A4MT29**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26a4mt29))-ho1:pcyA ([<u>**BBa\_K4354012**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k4354012) )-L3S2P21 ([<u>**BBa\_K2675031**</u>](https://share.google/pocPiJukHq9mm39e5)). Ho1 converts heme to biliverdin IXa, and PcyA subsequently reduces it to PCB. Fusing the two enzymes raises PCB production about 80 fold (Castillo-Hair et al. 2019). We used the shorter PtagC+RBS instead of Pveg and RBS0 to cut down repeated sequences and make Level 2 assembly easier .
2. Light Sensing ([BBa\_261XH2RS](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs)): PliaG (BBa\_K823000)-RBS0  (BBa\_26OSLRE4)- ccaS-m3 ([BBa\_26OSLRE4](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26oslre4))- B0015 (BBa\_B0015). This module expresses CcaSm3, the light sensor. Green light switches CcaS to an active state that passes a phosphate to CcaR, and red light switches it back.
3. Transduction ([BBa\_26BDO8AQ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq)): Pveg (BBa\_K143012) – RBS0 – ccaR (BBa\_K5431017) – B0015. When CcaS phosphorylates it under green light, CcaR binds the PcpcG2 promoter and activates transcription, and under red light it is likely dephosphorylated so that output switches off. Pveg keeps CcaR constitutively expressed, so light is the only input to the circuit. 
4. Light responsive ([BBa\_26DE5E2Q](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26de5e2q)): PcpcG2-veg – EEBD – RBS0 – SamyQ– AcdS 2.1– 6xHis ([BBa\_26TOGLX3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3)) – B0015. PcpcG2-veg is a strong promoter derived from Castillo-Hair et al. 2019, the Csn signal peptide directs ACC deaminase through the Sec pathway for secretion, where it degrades ACC, and the C-terminal 6xHis tag enables detection of the protein.

This complete construct was assembled by Golden gate assembly into the Level 2 vector pSTK-EXP2 with BsmBI enzyme

## About

* Biosafety level: S1
* Target organism: *Bacillus subtilis* \[168/WB800]
* Main purpose of use: light controlled expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis*
* Potential application: controlling the release of plant growth promoting protectants with green and red light. Users can set stress thresholds for each crop through a microcontroller based sensor without redesigning the entire genetic circuit

## Literature

**How the circuit works:** CcaS binds PCB through its GAF domain and is made in a green-light sensitive ground state. Absorbing green light switches it to an active state that autophosphorylates and passes the phosphate to CcaR. Phosphorylated CcaR activates the PcpcG2 output promoter. Red light returns CcaS to the ground state and probably causes CcaS to dephosphorylate CcaR, which turns output off (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019; Hirose et al., 2008). Because *B. subtilis* does not make PCB, the circuit needs all four modules on the same plasmid to work. 

**Why optogenetic:** Our original plan was to release engineered rhizobacteria that sensed stress themselves, which limits the usable stressors, and crops also differ in their thresholds. For example, heat stress in *Arabidopsis* starts at about 30–37 °C, whereas peanut tolerates about 35–40 °C. Using light as the only input lets the user program thresholds per crop without redesigning the circuit. 

**Differences from the published system:** Castillo-Hair et al. (2019) drove *ccaS* from the xylose-inducible PxylA and *ccaR* from the IPTG-inducible Phy-spank. We replaced both with constitutive promoters (PliaG and Pveg) so that light is the only input and no inducer dosing is needed. 

**Output module:** PcpcG2-veg is promoter from Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), in which the sequence after the −10 hexamer comes from the strong Pveg promoter while the CcaR binding site stays intact. In the original study this gave much higher output than PcpcG2-172. The EEBD (*E. coli* expression-blocking device) sits upstream of the RBS to stop leaky expression of the output gene in *E. coli* during cloning, before the construct is moved into *B. subtilis*. The output gene is a fusion of a Sec signal peptide, *P. putida acdS*, and a 6xHis tag. In the SamyQ version, 12 of the first 15 *acdS* codons were recoded to open up the mRNA structure around the start codon. 

## References

1. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Tabor, J. J. (2019). Optogenetic control of *Bacillus subtilis* gene expression. *Nature Communications*, 10, 3099.
2. Hirose, Y., Shimada, T., Narikawa, R., Katayama, M., & Ikeuchi, M. (2008). Cyanobacteriochrome CcaS is the green light receptor that induces the expression of phycobilisome linker protein. *PNAS*, 105(28), 9528–9533.
3. Caro-Astorga, J., Rogan, M., Malcı, K., Ming, H., Debenedictis, E., James, P., & Ellis, T. (2025). SubtiToolKit: A bioengineering kit for *Bacillus subtilis* and Gram-positive bacteria. *Trends in Biotechnology*, 43(6), 1446–1469.
4. Fernández, S., Ayora, S., & Alonso, J. C. (2000). *Bacillus subtilis* homologous recombination: Genes and products. *Research in Microbiology*, 151(6), 481–486.
5. Chen, Y.-J., et al. (2013). Characterization of 582 natural and synthetic terminators and quantification of their design constraints. *Nature Methods*, 10(7), 659–664.
6. Haller, D. J., Castillo-Hair, S. M., & Tabor, J. J. (2025). Optogenetic control of *B. subtilis* gene expression using the CcaSR system. *Methods in Molecular Biology*, 2840, 1–17.
7. Radeck, J., et al. (2013). The Bacillus BioBrick Box. *Journal of Biological Engineering*, 7, 29.

Using light as the only input lets the user program thresholds per crop without redesigning the circuit. 

**Differences from the published system:** Castillo-Hair et al. (2019) drove *ccaS* from the xylose-inducible PxylA and *ccaR* from the IPTG-inducible Phy-spank. We replaced both with constitutive promoters (PliaG and Pveg) so that light is the only input and no inducer dosing is needed. 

**Output module:** PcpcG2-veg is promoter from Castillo-Hair et al. (2019), in which the sequence after the −10 hexamer comes from the strong Pveg promoter while the CcaR binding site stays intact. In the original study this gave much higher output than PcpcG2-172. The EEBD (*E. coli* expression-blocking device) sits upstream of the RBS to stop leaky expression of the output gene in *E. coli* during cloning, before the construct is moved into *B. subtilis*. The output gene is a fusion of a Sec signal peptide, *P. putida acdS*, and a 6xHis tag. In the SamyQ version, 12 of the first 15 *acdS* codons were recoded to open up the mRNA structure around the start codon.

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

Each module was first built and sequence verified as a Level 1 transcription unit in the SubtiToolKit pSTK-1A, -1B, -1C, and -1D vectors (Caro-Astorga et al. 2025). The four sequence verified Level 1 units were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction into the pSTK-EXP2 Level 2 vector, in the order Module 1-Module 2-Module 3-Module 4. We tested two vectors to insert ratios, 1:5 and 1:7. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and clones were screened by colony PCR with primers specific to each module and sequence verified. The verified plasmid was then electroporated into *B. subtilis* 168 and WB800 at 2.1-2.3 kV 

Construct details:

* Composite insert: pSTK-EXP2-sfGFP-PtagC+RBS-Ho1:pcyA-L3S2P21-PliaG-RBS0-CcaSm3-B0015-Pveg-RBS0-CcaR-B0015-PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ:AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015 
* Vector: pSTK-EXP2 (Level 2 vector)
* Assembly method: Golden Gate Assembly (BsmbI)
* Vector:insert ratios tested: 1:5 and 1:7
* Thermal cycle

| Temperature         | Time    | Cycles     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ---------- |
| 42 degrees Celcius  | 5 min   | 45 cycles  |
| 16 degrees Celcius  | 5 min   |            |
| 55 degrees celsius  | 10 min  | 1 cycle    |
| 80 degrees Celcius  | 20 min  | 1 cycle    |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the Level 2 transformation were screened by colony PCR, with primers specific to each module, and products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A colony was a positive candidate only if it gave a band of the expected size for the modules . Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that all four modules are correct and in the right order. We checked every module because one module being positive doesn’t necessarily verify the state of the others. Constructs that were confirmed were then electroporated into *B. subtilis* and grown into liquid culture to initiate full functional runs in the LPA. 

| Primer      | Sequence                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| L2-pcyA-F   | GCG AAG CAT GGG CAG AAA GA     |
| L2-ccaSm3 R | GCG TTC TTG GTT TTG TCT GTG CC |
| L2-ccaSm3 F | GGG AAC AGG ACT CGG TTT AAT GG |
| L2-ccaR R   | CCA GCG GCA AAT CAT CCT CC     |
| L2-ccaR F   | GGT CCA TGG CAT TGG GTA TCG    |
| L2-SamyQ R  | GAA CGA AAC TGT CCG CTT TCG TT |

**Fig. 1. Colony PCR verification of the Level 2 CcasR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag construct.** Lanes 1 through 11 represent individual colonies screened using CcaSm3 fw and CcaR rv primers. The electrophoresis results highlight that lanes 1 through 11 yield a band around the expected size of 632 basepairs. 

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/ceb2e430-3a0a-4a10-8496-5d6acb63c0ea/68787dec5c522066ab3a008b06d1c5a2581dfda420e14af37e40128647249b32.avif)

**Fig. 2. Colony PCR verification of the Level 2 CcasR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag construct.** Lanes 1 represent individual colonies screened using Ho1:pcyA fw and Ccasm3 rv primers; Lanes 2 represent individual colonies screened using CcaSm3 fw and CcaR rv primers; and Lanes 3 represent colonies screened using CcaR fw and ACCD rv primers. The electrophoresis results indicate that lanes 1, 2 and 3 yield a single band around the expected sizes of 375, 632, and 441 basepairs accordingly.

**Fig.1. Level 2 optogenetic control of His-tagged ACC deaminase expression (ABDQ).** Cells were grown under green light (G), which is expected to activate ACCD expression, or red light (R), which served as the repressing control. Samples were collected 13 h and 16 h after light exposure and probed with an anti-His primary antibody. Lane M is the protein marker ladder. Band intensities were similar across all lanes, so ACCD was produced steadily and at comparable levels under both wavelengths under the conditions tested. 



**Fig.2. Optogenetic induced time-course of ACC deaminase expression under secondary regulation (ABDQ).** Western blot of His-tagged ACCD in *B. subtilis* cultures that were kept in the dark overnight (16 h) and then exposed to green light for 3, 6, or 8 h (O8). Lane M is the protein molecular weight marker. Probing with an anti-His primary antibody showed ACCD at all time points, with similar levels throughout.

sections.title: Application
sections.original:
The Level 2 construct ccaSR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag (BBa\_2654HAF3) shows that *Bacillus subtilis* can sense light and respond to it on its own. All four modules sit on a single plasmid. The first makes the chromophore PCB, the second expresses the sensor kinase CcaS-m3, the third expresses the response regulator CcaR, and the fourth secretes ACC deaminase (AcdS 2.1) when green light is present. Because *B. subtilis* does not make PCB, the circuit only works with all four modules together.

We tested this in *B. subtilis* WB800 in the LPA (light plate apparatus) under green and red light at different intensities. Western blots showed ACCD signal increasing over time under green light, but not under red light. This is the proof of concept for the whole design: light is the only input, and no inducer needs to be added.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.original:
#### Use in plant protection

The aim is to release plant-protective proteins only when and where they are needed. A secreted ACC deaminase lowers stress ethylene around roots, so it could be used as part of a plant-growth-promoting bioprotectant. Light as the only input offers a practical advantage over circuits that sense stress themselves. Crops differ in their stress thresholds (for example, heat stress starts at about 30 to 37 °C in *Arabidopsis* but about 35 to 40 °C in peanut), and a self-sensing strain would have to be redesigned for each stressor and each crop. With light control, a user can set thresholds for each crop through a microcontroller-based sensor that switches the light, without redesigning the genetic circuit. This is the role the circuit plays in our bioreactor system.

#### A modular platform for other protectants

Modules 1 to 3 form a reusable light-sensing chassis, and only Module 4 defines the output. Any of our protectant cassettes can in principle be placed behind PcpcG2-veg:

* **AcdS** lowers ethylene levels. This is the version built and tested in the full circuit.
* **LEA14** protects cellular structures under environmental stress. We did not build the light-responsive Module 4 with LEA14. Instead, we characterized the constitutive LEA14 version to see how it would behave in the whole system, and it also protects plants facing salinity stress. This avoids repeating the same assembly, since ccaSR-AcdS already demonstrates that the concept works.
* **BoPep4**, a broccoli plant elicitor peptide, activates plant defense responses.

Our constitutive constructs, which use Pveg in place of the light switch, give the maximal secretion and production of each protectant. They also serve as a benchmark for the light-controlled version.

#### Beyond our project

Replacing the xylose-inducible and IPTG-inducible promoters of the published CcaSR system (Castillo-Hair et al., 2019) with constitutive ones means no inducer dosing is required. Other teams can reuse the four-module Level 2 plasmid for any secreted protein, simply by exchanging the output cassette. This makes light-controlled secretion in *B. subtilis* usable beyond plant protection, for example for other enzymes or peptides that should be produced on demand.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS: [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a composite transcription unit with three elements, in this order:

* **Pveg (**Bba\_K143012**):** a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction. 
* **EEBD-RBS0 (**[BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)**):** A composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*
* **SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag (**[BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)**):** a translational fusion of three elements:
  1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
  2. **AcdS 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_262YYNPV**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-262yynpv)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303) , with its native start codon and stop codon removed  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from AcdS wild-type ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
  3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.
* **B0015** (BBa\_B0015): A high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of ACC deaminase
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**Rationale.** ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of ethylene, and so can lower the ethylene levels that inhibit plant growth under stress (Hontzeas et al., 2004; Shah et al., 1998). The Csn signal peptide exports the enzyme from the cell, and the C-terminal 6x Histag allows detection and purification. The AcdS sequence comes from Q5PWZ8 (UniProt Consortium, n.d.; GenBank CP053102.1).

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo rather than promoter strength. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *E. coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts, so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## References

1\. UniProt Consortium. (n.d.). Q5PWZ8. UniProt. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from UniProt entry Q5PWZ8

2\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). Expression and characterization of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase from the rhizobacterium *Pseudomonas putida* UW4: A key enzyme in bacterial plant growth promotion. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, 1703(1), 11–19. PubMed. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

3\. Shah, S., Li, J., Moffatt, B. A., & Glick, B. R. (1998). Isolation and characterization of ACC deaminase genes from two different plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. Canadian Journal of Microbiology, 44(9), 833–843. [https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074](https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074)

4\. Glick, B. R., Penrose, D. M., & Li, J. (1998). A model for the lowering of plant ethylene concentrations by plant growth-promoting bacteria. Journal of Theoretical Biology, 190(1), 63–68. [https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532](https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532)

5\. Castillo-Hair, S. M., Baerman, E. A., Fujita, M., Igoshin, O. A., & Voigt, C. A. (2019). Optogenetic control of *Bacillus subtilis* gene expression. Nature Communications, 10, Article 3099. [https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10906-6)

  2. **AcdS 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_262YYNPV**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-262yynpv)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303) , with its native start codon and stop codon removed  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from AcdS wild-type ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
  3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.
* **B0015** (BBa\_B0015): A high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of ACC deaminase
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**Rationale.** ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of ethylene, and so can lower the ethylene levels that inhibit plant growth under stress (Hontzeas et al., 2004; Shah et al., 1998). The Csn signal peptide exports the enzyme from the cell, and the C-terminal 6x Histag allows detection and purification. The AcdS sequence comes from Q5PWZ8 (UniProt Consortium, n.d.; GenBank CP053102.1).

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo rather than promoter strength. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *E. coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts, so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## References

1\. UniProt Consortium. (n.d.). Q5PWZ8. UniProt. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from UniProt entry Q5PWZ8

2\. Hontzeas, N., Zoidakis, J., Glick, B. R., & Abu-Omar, M. M. (2004). Expression and characterization of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase from the rhizobacterium *Pseudomonas putida* UW4: A key enzyme in bacterial plant growth promotion. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, 1703(1), 11–19. PubMed. [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbapap.2004.09.015)

3\. Shah, S., Li, J., Moffatt, B. A., & Glick, B. R. (1998). Isolation and characterization of ACC deaminase genes from two different plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. Canadian Journal of Microbiology, 44(9), 833–843. [https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074](https://doi.org/10.1139/w98-074)

4\. Glick, B. R., Penrose, D. M., & Li, J. (1998). A model for the lowering of plant ethylene concentrations by plant growth-promoting bacteria. Journal of Theoretical Biology, 190(1), 63–68. [https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532](https://doi.org/10.1006/jtbi.1997.0532)

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* **Composite insert:** Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag – B0015, \[1848 bp]
* **Level 1 vector:** pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* **Template:** synthesized fragments assembled together
* **Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification):** 60 °C
* **Assembly method (Level 1):** Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* **Thermal cycle:**

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesized fragment using primers SamyQ F and ACCD R. Each primer carries a 5′ ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for level 0 vector entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the SamyQ start codon) at the 5′ end and TGTC at the 3′ end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pSTK-0C-sfGFP and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26TOGLX3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                         |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                    |
| SamyQ F        | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGATTC AAAAACGAAAGCGGAC |
| ACCD R         | ATATATGAAGACATGAGGGGTCTCATGTCTTAATGATGATGATGATGAT  |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                             |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with backbone primers primers flanking the CDS insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[1984 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

***Figure 1.*** **Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015.** 1 of 1 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1984 bp]).

***Figure 2.*** **Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

BBa_26XZYM10.title: PtagC+RBS-Ho1:pcyA-L3S2P21
BBa_26XZYM10.description: The PCB Production Module supplies the chromophore required for light sensing. It consists of the H*o1-pcyA* CDS, along with the PtagC+RBS composite promoter and RBS and the L3S2P21 terminator, which converts endogenous heme into phycocyanobilin (PCB), the chromophore necessary for CcaS photoreceptor activity. PCB enables the light-sensing system to detect and respond to green light.

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

The PCB Production Module supplies the chromophore required for light sensing.

The part is a composite transcription unit with three elements, in this order:

* **PtagC+RBS (**[<u>**BBa\_26A4MT29**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26a4mt29)**):** a promoter and ribosome binding site that controls both transcription and translation of the downstream coding sequence.
* **Ho1-pcyA (**[<u>**BBa\_K4354012**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k4354012) **):** a fusion CDS of heme oxygenase-1 (Ho1) and phycocyanobilin:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PcyA). Ho1 converts endogenous heme to biliverdin IXα, and PcyA reduces biliverdin IXα to PCB. 
* **L3S2P21 (**[<u>**BBa\_K2675031**</u>](https://share.google/pocPiJukHq9mm39e5)**):** a strong synthetic intrinsic (Rho-independent) terminator from the synthetic terminator library of Chen et al. (2013), which ends transcription and limits read-through into neighboring units.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

**Design considerations:**

*Why PCB must be supplied:* CcaS is a cyanobacteriochrome that senses green and red light only when it binds PCB. *B. subtilis* does not naturally make PCB, so without this module the CcaSR system cannot respond to light. Fusing Ho1 and pcyA into a single CDS allows both biosynthetic steps from one gene, which keeps the module compact and the two enzymes stoichiometrically matched. PtagC+RBS presented a shorter length in base pairs, therefore allowing easier cloning into a level 2 transcriptional unit. Because there was an ambiguity on homologous recombination, it was used as an alternative to Pveg and RBS0, as the plasmid was already amplified in our collection.

*Expression context:* Heme is an endogenous substrate in *B. subtilis*, so the module needs no added precursor. Ferredoxin is required as the electron donor for PcyA. 

*Design:* The full CDS was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesized fragment using primers Csn F and ACCD R. Each primer carries a 5′ ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for Level 0 entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the Csn start codon) at the 5′ end and TGTC at the 3′ end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pGEM-T Easy and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 (BBa\_26V6CPEV), Csn-AcdS-Histag (BBa\_26NXOP7S) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (Caro-Astorga et al., 2025), a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Intracellular biosynthesis of phycocyanobilin (PCB), the chromophore required for CcaS photoreceptor activity, in the host *B. subtilis*.
* **Potential application:** Enabling green/red light-responsive gene expression through the CcaSR system, as the light-sensing component of a stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor for plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

### **References**

1. CcaSR green red light-responsive system for transcriptional control in B. subtilis (Haller et al., 2025; 10.1007/978-1-0716-40)\*\* 
2. Chen, Y.-J., Liu, P., Nielsen, A. A. K., et al. (2013). Characterization of 582 natural and synthetic terminators and quantification of their design constraints. *Nature Methods*, 10(7), 659–664.
3. [<u>**BBa\_K4354012**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k4354012)
4. [<u>**BBa\_K2675031**</u>](https://share.google/pocPiJukHq9mm39e5)
5. Caro-Astorga, J., Rogan, M., Malcı, K., Ming, H., Debenedictis, E., James, P., & Ellis, T. (2025). SubtiToolKit: A bioengineering kit for *Bacillus subtilis* and Gram-positive bacteria. *Trends in Biotechnology, 43*(6), 1446–1469.[ <u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004</u>](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.02.004)

sections.original:

sections.title: Design
sections.original:
## Overview

This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14)from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup. 

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **Csn signal peptide:** the N-terminal Sec-dependent signal peptide of *B. subtilis* chitosanase (gene *csn*), which directs the protein to the secretion pathway and is cleaved off during export. Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **LEA14 (**[<u>BBa\_26LTB0W1</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ltb0w1)**):** This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) from [<u>*Arabidopsis thaliana*</u>](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O03983/entry) with its native start codon and stop codon removed.  
3. **6x Histag:** This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation. Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800]
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of LEA14 in the host *B. subtilis*
* **Potential application:** Protecting cellular structures and maintaining cellular stability under environmental stress conditions.

## References

1. Goyal, K., Walton, L. J., & Tunnacliffe, A. (2005). LEA proteins prevent protein aggregation due to water stress. *Biochemical Journal, 388(1)*, 151–157. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1042/bj20041931</u>](https://doi.org/10.1042/bj20041931)  
2. Hundertmark, M., Hincha, D. K., & Thalhammer, A. (2008). LEA (late embryogenesis abundant) proteins and their encoding genes in *Arabidopsis thaliana*. *BMC Genomics, 9*, Article 118. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-9-118</u>](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-9-118)  
3. Jia, F., Qi, S., Li, H., Liu, P., Li, P., Wu, C., Zheng, C., & Huang, J. (2014). Overexpression of late embryogenesis abundant 14 enhances *Arabidopsis* salt stress tolerance. *Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications, 454(4)*, 505–511. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2014.10.136</u>](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2014.10.136)  
4. Mertens, J., Aliyu, H., & Cowan, D. A. (2018). LEA proteins and the evolution of the WHy domain. *Applied and Environmental Microbiology, 84(15)*, Article e00539-18. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.00539-18</u>](https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.00539-18)  
5. Singh, S., Cornilescu, C. C., Tyler, R. C., Cornilescu, G., Tonelli, M., Lee, M. S., & Markley, J. L. (2005). Solution structure of a late embryogenesis abundant protein (LEA14) from *Arabidopsis thaliana*, a cellular stress-related protein. *Protein Science, 14(10)*, 2601–2609. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1110/ps.051579205</u>](https://doi.org/10.1110/ps.051579205)  
6. Wang, J. W., Squire, H. J., Goh, N. S., Ni, H. M., Lien, E., Wong, C., González-Grandío, E., & Landry, M. P. (2023). Delivered complementation in planta (DCIP) enables measurement of peptide-mediated protein delivery efficiency in plants. *Communications Biology, 6(1)*, Article 829. [<u>https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-023-05191-5</u>](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-023-05191-5)

sections.title: Experiment
sections.original:
## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The Csn-LEA14-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-Csn-LEA14-Histag. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the Csn-LEA14-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

Construct details:

* **Insert:** Csn signal peptide – LEA14 – 6x Histag, \[576 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Csn F       | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGAAAA TCAGTATGCAAAAAGCA |
| LEA R       | ATATATGAAGACATGAGGGGTCTCATGTCTTAA TGATGATGATGATGAT  |

* **Template:** synthetized fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-Csn-LEA14-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the Csn and STK primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the Csn-LEA14-Histag insert \[576 bp] plus the vector sequence between the Histag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[811 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, LEA14 coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/6e46f42a-045c-4116-9c2a-6146c4330d7d/2438a0dda56a65c53ee6b971ee84ca082b5adaef14b4777a95a1194d2cd9c618.avif)

Figure 1. **Colony PCR of pSTK-0C-Csn-LEA14-Histag.** The figure indicates that 16 of 16 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[811 bp])

Figure 2. **Clone 2 was sent for sequencing with a silent mutation (G381A)**

Figure 3. **Clone 10 was sent for sequencing, but had a point mutation at 299.**

Figure 4. **Clone 16 was sequence-verified and used for downstream experiments.**

sections.title: Application
sections.original:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of the composite part:

* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-LEA14-Histag-B0015** ([<u>BBa\_26SG0NQQ</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26sg0nqq)): this Protectant Module constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS0, and terminator B0015.
